original_iast: ataḥ- saṃsāra-viṣaya-vṛkṣasya dve eva rasavat phale | kāvyāmṛta-rasāsvādaḥ saṅgamaḥ sajjanaiḥ saha
transliterated_devanagari: अतः- संसार-विषय-वृक्षस्य द्वे एव रसवत् फले | काव्यामृत-रसास्वादः सङ्गमः सज्जनइः सह
full_translation: Therefore, in the world, there are only two juicy fruits of the tree of subjects: the tasting of poetic nectar and the union with the virtuous.

original_iast: aparaṃ ca- sat-saṅgaḥ keśave bhaktir gaṅgāmbhasi nimajjanam | asāre khalu saṃsāre trīṇi sārāṇi bhāvayet
transliterated_devanagari: अपरं च- सत-सङ्गः केशवे भक्तिर् गङ्गाम्भसि निमज्जनम् | असारे खलु संसारे त्रीणि साराणि भावयेत्

word_by_word_translation.translation: in the waters of the Ganges

full_translation: Moreover, true association with Keshava, immersion in the waters of the Ganges, indeed, in this transient world, one should contemplate the three essentials.

original_iast: arthāḥ pāda-rajopamā giri-nadī-vegopamaṃ yauvanam āyuṣyaṃ jala-bindu-lola-capalaṃ phenopamaṃ jīvanam | dharmaṃ yo na karoti niścala-matiḥ svargārgalodghāṭanaṃ paścāt-tāpa-hato jarā-pariṇataḥ śokāgninā dahyate
transliterated_devanagari: अर्थाः पाद-रजोपमा गिरि-नदी-वेगोपमं यउवनम् आयुष्यं जल-बिन्दु-लोल-चपलं फेनोपमं जीवनम् | धर्मं यो न करोति निश्चल-मतिः स्वर्गार्गलोद्घाटनं पश्चात-ताप-हतो जरा-परिणतः शोकाग्निना दह्यते
full_translation: The meanings are like the dust of the feet, the mountains, the rivers, the speed of youth, the life of a drop of water, trembling and fickle like foam. Life is the duty of one who does not act with a steady mind. After the opening of the heavenly abode, old age, killed by the heat, is transformed and burned by the fire of sorrow.

original_iast: upārjitānāṃ vittānāṃ tyāga eva hi rakṣaṇam | taḍāgodara-saṃsthānāṃ parīvāhaivāmbhasām
transliterated_devanagari: उपार्जितानां वित्तानां त्याग एव हि रक्षणम् | तडागोदर-संस्थानां परीवाहइवाम्भसाम्
full_translation: Indeed, the protection of acquired wealth is only through renunciation, like the flow of waters from the depths of a lake.

original_iast: anyac ca- yad adho 'dhaḥ kṣitau vittaṃ nicakhāna mitampacaḥ | tad-adho nilayaṃ gantuṃ cakre panthānam agrataḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- यद् अधो ऽधः क्षितउ वित्तं निचखान मितम्पचः | तद-अधो निलयं गन्तुं चक्रे पन्थानम् अग्रतः
full_translation: Also, that which was dug up below the earth as wealth, made a path to go to the abode below.

original_iast: yataḥ- nija-saukhyaṃ nirundhāno yo dhanārjanam icchati | parārtha-bhāra-vāhīva sa kleśasyaiva bhājanam
transliterated_devanagari: यतः- निज-सउख्यं निरुन्धानो यो धनार्जनम् इच्छति | परार्थ-भार-वाहीव स क्लेशस्यइव भाजनम्
full_translation: From whom one restrains one's own happiness, who desires wealth acquisition for the sake of others, that person is like a bearer of a burden, akin to a vessel of suffering.

original_iast: tathā coktaṃ- dānopabhoga-hīnena dhanena dhanino yadi | bhavāmaḥ kiṃ na tenaiva dhanena dhanino vayam
transliterated_devanagari: तथा चोक्तं- दानोपभोग-हीनेन धनेन धनिनो यदि | भवामः किं न तेनइव धनेन धनिनो वयम्
full_translation: Thus it is said: if we become wealthy by the enjoyment of giving, what is it that we are not, indeed, by that wealth of the wealthy?

original_iast: dhanena kiṃ yo na dadāti nāśnute balena kiṃ yaś ca ripūn na yādhatte | śrutena kiṃ yo na ca dharmam ācaret kim ātmanā yo na jitendriyo bhavet
transliterated_devanagari: धनेन किं यो न ददाति नाश्नुते बलेन किं यश् च रिपून् न याधत्ते | श्रुतेन किं यो न च धर्मम् आचरेत् किम् आत्मना यो न जितेन्द्रियो भवेत्
full_translation: What use is wealth to one who does not give? What use is strength to one who does not overcome enemies? What use is knowledge to one who does not practice righteousness? What use is it for a person to be self-controlled if they are not a master of their senses?

original_iast: anyac ca- asambhogena sāmānyaṃ kṛpaṇasya dhanaṃ paraiḥ | asyedam iti sambandho hānau duḥkhena gamyate
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- असम्भोगेन सामान्यं कृपणस्य धनं परइः | अस्येदम् इति सम्बन्धो हानउ दुःखेन गम्यते
full_translation: And also, the wealth of the miser is commonly attained by others through non-enjoyment; thus, the connection is that loss is attained through suffering.

original_iast: api ca- na devāya na viprāya na bandhubhyo na cātmane | kṛpaṇasya dhanaṃ yāti vahni-taskara-pārthivaiḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अपि च- न देवाय न विप्राय न बन्धुभ्यो न चात्मने | कृपणस्य धनं याति वह्नि-तस्कर-पार्थिवइः
full_translation: Indeed, wealth does not go to the god, nor to the learned, nor to relatives, nor to oneself; it goes to the fire, the thief of the earthly.

original_iast: dānaṃ priya-vāk-sahitaṃ jñānam agarvaṃ kṣamānvitaṃ sauryam | tyāgaṃ sahitaṃ ca vittaṃ durlabham etac catur bhadram
transliterated_devanagari: दानं प्रिय-वाक-सहितं ज्ञानम् अगर्वं क्षमान्वितं सउर्यम् | त्यागं सहितं च वित्तं दुर्लभम् एतच् चतुर् भद्रम्
full_translation: A donation, beloved speech together with knowledge, without arrogance, endowed with forgiveness, with valor, renunciation together with wealth—this is the clever auspiciousness.

original_iast: uktaṃ ca- kartavyaḥ sañcayo nityaṃ na tu kāryo 'tisañcayaḥ | atisañcaya-śīlo 'yaṃ dhanuṣā jambuko hataḥ
transliterated_devanagari: उक्तं च- कर्तव्यः सञ्चयो नित्यं न तु कार्यो ऽतिसञ्चयः | अतिसञ्चय-शीलो ऽयं धनुषा जम्बुको हतः
full_translation: It is said that the duty is to collect regularly, but not to engage in excessive accumulation; this character of excessive accumulation has led to the jackal being killed by the bow.

original_iast: jalam agnir viṣaṃ śastaṃ kṣud vyādhiḥ patanaṃ gireḥ | nimittaṃ kiñcid āsādya dehī prāṇair vimucyate
transliterated_devanagari: जलम् अग्निर् विषं शस्तं क्षुद् व्याधिः पतनं गिरेः | निमित्तं किञ्चिद् आसाद्य देही प्राणइर् विमुच्यते
full_translation: Water, fire, poison, weapon, hunger, disease, the fall of a mountain—having attained some cause, the embodied being is liberated by life.

original_iast: athavā- acintitāni duḥkhāni yathaivāyānti dehinām | sukhāny api tathā manye daivam atrātiricyate
transliterated_devanagari: अथवा- अचिन्तितानि दुःखानि यथइवायान्ति देहिनाम् | सुखान्य् अपि तथा मन्ये दइवम् अत्रातिरिच्यते
full_translation: Or, unthought-of sufferings indeed come to embodied beings; I think that happiness also transcends the divine here.

original_iast: māsam ekaṃ naro yāti dvau māsau mṛga-śūkarau | ahir ekaṃ dinaṃ yāti adya bhakṣyo dhanurguṇaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: मासम् एकं नरो याति द्वउ मासउ मृग-शूकरउ | अहिर् एकं दिनं याति अद्य भक्ष्यो धनुर्गुणः
full_translation: A man goes for one month; for two months, a deer, a boar, and a snake go. Today, the qualities of the bow are edible.

original_iast: yad dadāti yad aśnāti tad eva dhanino dhanam | anye mṛtasya krīḍanti dārair api dhanair api
transliterated_devanagari: यद् ददाति यद् अश्नाति तद् एव धनिनो धनम् | अन्ये मृतस्य क्रीडन्ति दारइर् अपि धनइर् अपि
full_translation: That which gives and that which takes, indeed, is the wealth of the wealthy; others play with the dead, both with wives and with wealth.

original_iast: kiṃ ca- yad dadāsi viśiṣṭebhyo yac cāśnāsi dine dine | tat te vittam ahaṃ manye śeṣaṃ kasyāpi rakṣasi
transliterated_devanagari: किं च- यद् ददासि विशिष्टेभ्यो यच् चाश्नासि दिने दिने | तत् ते वित्तम् अहं मन्ये शेषं कस्यापि रक्षसि
full_translation: What you give to the distinguished and what you eat day by day, I think that wealth of yours is the remainder that you protect for anyone.

original_iast: nāprāyam abhivāñchanti naṣṭaṃ necchanti śocitum | āpatsv api na muhyanti narāḥ paṇḍita-buddhayaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: नाप्रायम् अभिवाञ्छन्ति नष्टं नेच्छन्ति शोचितुम् | आपत्स्व् अपि न मुह्यन्ति नराः पण्डित-बुद्धयः
full_translation: Wise men are not generally desirous of lamenting over what is lost; even in calamities, they are not bewildered.

original_iast: śāstrāṇy adhītyāpi bhavanti mūrkhā yas tu kriyāvān puruṣaḥ sa vidvān | sucintitaṃ cauṣadham āturāṇāṃ na nāma-mātreṇa karoty arogam
transliterated_devanagari: शास्त्राण्य् अधीत्यापि भवन्ति मूर्खा यस् तु क्रियावान् पुरुषः स विद्वान् | सुचिन्तितं चउषधम् आतुराणां न नाम-मात्रेण करोत्य् अरोगम्
full_translation: A person who merely studies scriptures becomes a fool; however, a man who acts is indeed learned and provides a well-considered medicine for the sick, not just by name.

original_iast: na svalpam apy adhyavasāya-bhīroḥ karoti vijñāna-vidhir guṇaṃ hi | andhasya kiṃ hasta-tala-sthito 'pi prakāśayaty artham iha pradīpaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: न स्वल्पम् अप्य् अध्यवसाय-भीरोः करोति विज्ञान-विधिर् गुणं हि | अन्धस्य किं हस्त-तल-स्थितो ऽपि प्रकाशयत्य् अर्थम् इह प्रदीपः
full_translation: Even a small determination of the brave indeed illuminates the meaning, just as a lamp situated on the surface of the hand can enlighten the blind.

original_iast: sukham āpatitaṃ sevyaṃ duḥkham āpatitaṃ tathā | cakravat parivartante duḥkhāni ca sukhāni ca
transliterated_devanagari: सुखम् आपतितं सेव्यं दुःखम् आपतितं तथा | चक्रवत् परिवर्तन्ते दुःखानि च सुखानि च
full_translation: Happiness arises to be experienced, and suffering also arises; thus, like a wheel, sufferings and happinesses revolve.

original_iast: aparaṃ ca- nipānam iva maṇḍūkāḥ saraḥ pūrṇam ivāṇḍajāḥ | sodyogaṃ naram āyānti vivaśāḥ sarva-sampadaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अपरं च- निपानम् इव मण्डूकाः सरः पूर्णम् इवाण्डजाः | सोद्योगं नरम् आयान्ति विवशाः सर्व-सम्पदः
full_translation: Another situation is like frogs in a full lake, coming helplessly to a man with effort, like eggs.

original_iast: api ca- utsāha-saṃpannam adīrgha-sūtraṃ kriyā-vidhijñaṃ vyasaneṣv asaktam | śūraṃ kṛtajñaṃ dṛḍha-sauhṛdaṃ ca- lakṣmīḥ svayaṃ vāñchati vāsa-hetoḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अपि च- उत्साह-संपन्नम् अदीर्घ-सूत्रं क्रिया-विधिज्ञं व्यसनेष्व् असक्तम् | शूरं कृतज्ञं दृढ-सउहृदं च- लक्ष्मीः स्वयं वाञ्छति वास-हेतोः
full_translation: Moreover, wealth (Lakshmi) herself desires a person endowed with enthusiasm, who is not long-winded, knowledgeable in actions, unattached in troubles, brave, grateful, firm, and friendly, for the purpose of residence.

original_iast: vināpy arthair dhīraḥ spṛśati bahumānonnati-padaṃ samāyukto 'py arthaiḥ paribhava-padaṃ yāti kṛpaṇaḥ | svabhāvād udbhūtāṃ guṇa-samudayāvāpti-viṣayāṃ dyutiṃ saiṃhīṃ śvā kiṃ dhṛta-kanaka-mālo 'pi labhate
transliterated_devanagari: विनाप्य् अर्थइर् धीरः स्पृशति बहुमानोन्नति-पदं समायुक्तो ऽप्य् अर्थइः परिभव-पदं याति कृपणः | स्वभावाद् उद्भूतां गुण-समुदयावाप्ति-विषयां द्युतिं सइंहीं श्वा किं धृत-कनक-मालो ऽपि लभते
full_translation: Without wealth, the wise man touches the position of great honor and advancement; even when associated with wealth, he goes to the position of defeat. By nature, the miser, arising from the qualities, attains the glory of the subject. What does the dog, even holding a garland of gold, receive?

original_iast: kiṃ ca- dhanavān iti hi madas te kiṃ gata-vibhavo viṣādam upayāsi | kara-nihata-kanduka-samāḥ pātotpātā manuṣyāṇām
transliterated_devanagari: किं च- धनवान् इति हि मदस् ते किं गत-विभवो विषादम् उपयासि | कर-निहत-कन्दुक-समाः पातोत्पाता मनुष्याणाम्
full_translation: What indeed is the use of being wealthy if your pride leads you to sorrow? You approach with a hand struck down, equal to a ball that falls, like that of humans.

original_iast: anyac ca- vṛtty-arthaṃ nāticeṣṭate sā hi dhātraiva nirmitā | garbhād utpatite jantau mātuḥ prasravataḥ stanau
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- वृत्त्य-अर्थं नातिचेष्टते सा हि धात्रइव निर्मिता | गर्भाद् उत्पतिते जन्तउ मातुः प्रस्रवतः स्तनउ

word_by_word_translation.translation: does not exert too much effort

full_translation: And also, by occupation, she does not exert too much effort; indeed, she is created like a nurse, flowing from the breast of the mother upon the birth of the creature.

original_iast: api ca sakhe śṛṇu- yena śuklī-kṛtā haṃsāḥ śukāś ca haritīkṛtāḥ | mayūrāś citritā yena sa te vṛttiṃ vidhāsyati
transliterated_devanagari: अपि च सखे शृणु- येन शुक्ली-कृता हंसाः शुकाश् च हरितीकृताः | मयूराश् चित्रिता येन स ते वृत्तिं विधास्यति
full_translation: O friend, listen to whom the white one has made swans, and the parrot has made green, and the peacocks have been decorated; by whom he will establish your activity.

original_iast: janayanty arjane duḥkhaṃ tāpayanti vipattiṣu | mohayanti ca sampattau katham arthāḥ sukhāvahāḥ
transliterated_devanagari: जनयन्त्य् अर्जने दुःखं तापयन्ति विपत्तिषु | मोहयन्ति च सम्पत्तउ कथम् अर्थाः सुखावहाः
full_translation: They generate suffering in earning, cause distress in calamities, and delude in prosperity; how do the meanings bring happiness?

original_iast: aparaṃ ca- dharmārdhaṃ yasya vittehā varaṃ tasya nirīhatā | prakṣālanād dhi paṅkasya dūrād asparśanaṃ varam
transliterated_devanagari: अपरं च- धर्मार्धं यस्य वित्तेहा वरं तस्य निरीहता | प्रक्षालनाद् धि पङ्कस्य दूराद् अस्पर्शनं वरम्
full_translation: Another excellent form of righteous wealth is the detachment from wealth, indeed, not touching the mud from afar is excellent.

original_iast: yataḥ- yathāāmiṣam ākāśe pakṣibhiḥ śvāpadair bhuvi | bhakṣyate salile matsyais tathā sarvatra vittavān
transliterated_devanagari: यतः- यथाआमिषम् आकाशे पक्षिभिः श्वापदइर् भुवि | भक्ष्यते सलिले मत्स्यइस् तथा सर्वत्र वित्तवान्
full_translation: Just as flesh is eaten in the sky by birds, on the earth by beasts, and in the water by fish, so too is wealth found everywhere.

original_iast: anyac ca- rājataḥ salilād agneś corataḥ svajanād api | bhayam arthavatāṃ nityaṃ mṛtyoḥ prāṇa-bhṛtām iva
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- राजतः सलिलाद् अग्नेश् चोरतः स्वजनाद् अपि | भयम् अर्थवतां नित्यं मृत्योः प्राण-भृताम् इव
full_translation: And also, there is fear from the king, from water, from fire, from a thief, even from one's own kin; always, there is fear like that of death for those who sustain life.

original_iast: tathā hi- janmani kleśa-bahule kiṃ nu duḥkham ataḥ param | icchā-sampad yato nāsti yac cecchā na nivartate
transliterated_devanagari: तथा हि- जन्मनि क्लेश-बहुले किं नु दुःखम् अतः परम् | इच्छा-सम्पद् यतो नास्ति यच् चेच्छा न निवर्तते
full_translation: Indeed, in birth, there is abundant suffering; therefore, what sorrow is there beyond desire? From which wealth is there that does not cease when there is a wish?

original_iast: anyac ca bhrātaḥ śṛṇu- dhanaṃ tāvad asulabhaṃ labdhaṃ kṛcchreṇa pālyate | labdha-nāśo yathā mṛtyus tasmād etan na cintayet
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च भ्रातः शृणु- धनं तावद् असुलभं लब्धं कृच्छ्रेण पाल्यते | लब्ध-नाशो यथा मृत्युस् तस्माद् एतन् न चिन्तयेत्
full_translation: Also, brother, listen: wealth that is not easily obtained is maintained with difficulty; just as loss is like death. Therefore, one should not think about this.

original_iast: sā tṛṣṇā cet parityaktā ko daridraḥ ka īśvaraḥ | tasyāś cet prasaro datto dāsyaṃ ca śirasi sthitam
transliterated_devanagari: सा तृष्णा चेत् परित्यक्ता को दरिद्रः क ईश्वरः | तस्याश् चेत् प्रसरो दत्तो दास्यं च शिरसि स्थितम्
full_translation: If that desire is abandoned, who is poor? What God is there? If servitude is given, it is established on the head.

original_iast: aparaṃ ca- yad yad eva hi vāñcheta tato vāñchā pravartate | prāpta evārthataḥ so 'rtho yato vāñchā nivartate
transliterated_devanagari: अपरं च- यद् यद् एव हि वाञ्छेत ततो वाञ्छा प्रवर्तते | प्राप्त एवार्थतः सो ऽर्थो यतो वाञ्छा निवर्तते
full_translation: Furthermore, whatever one indeed desires, from that desire arises; when that is obtained, indeed, it is in terms of meaning that desire ceases.

original_iast: āmraṇāntāḥ praṇayāḥ kopāś ca kṣaṇa-bhaṅgurāḥ | parityāgāś ca niḥsaṅgā na bhavanti mahātmanām
transliterated_devanagari: आम्रणान्ताः प्रणयाः कोपाश् च क्षण-भङ्गुराः | परित्यागाश् च निःसङ्गा न भवन्ति महात्मनाम्
full_translation: The affections, anger, and transient moments of abandonment do not affect the great souls.

original_iast: santa eva satāṃ nityam āpad-uddharaṇa-kṣamāḥ | gajānāṃ paṅka-magnānāṃ gajā eva dhurandharāḥ
transliterated_devanagari: सन्त एव सतां नित्यम् आपद-उद्धरण-क्षमाः | गजानां पङ्क-मग्नानां गजा एव धुरन्धराः
full_translation: Indeed, the elephants that are capable of rescuing the virtuous from calamities are the great bearers, even when they are immersed in the mud.

original_iast: ślāghyaḥ sa eko bhuvi mānavānāṃ sa uttamaḥ sat-puruṣaḥ sa dhanyaḥ | yasyārthino vā śaraṇāgatā vā nāśāvibhaṅgā vimukhāḥ prayānti
transliterated_devanagari: श्लाघ्यः स एको भुवि मानवानां स उत्तमः सत-पुरुषः स धन्यः | यस्यार्थिनो वा शरणागता वा नाशाविभङ्गा विमुखाः प्रयान्ति

word_by_word_translation.translation: those who are not broken by destruction

full_translation: He is indeed praiseworthy; he is one among humans in this world, the best among good men, blessed is he whose seekers or those who have taken refuge, or those who are not broken by destruction, turn away.

original_iast: lobhād vātha bhayād vāpi yas tyajec charaṇāgatam | brahma-hatyā-samaṃ tasya pāpam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: लोभाद् वाथ भयाद् वापि यस् त्यजेच् छरणागतम् | ब्रह्म-हत्या-समं तस्य पापम् आहुर् मनीषिणः

word_by_word_translation.translation: the one who has taken refuge

full_translation: They say that the sin of killing Brahman is equal to that of a person who abandons the one who has taken refuge, whether out of greed or fear.

original_iast: aurasaṃ kṛta-sambandhaṃ tathā vaṃśa-kramāgatam | rakṣakaṃ vyasanebhyaś ca mitraṃ jñeyaṃ catur-vidham
transliterated_devanagari: औरसं कृत-सम्बन्धं तथा वंश-क्रमागतम् | रक्षकं व्यसनेभ्यश् च मित्रं ज्ञेयं चतुर-विधम्
full_translation: A friend who is a protector, born of the same womb, and related by lineage, is to be known in a clever manner, especially in times of misfortune.

original_iast: ambhāṃsi jala-jantūnāṃ durgaṃ durga-nivāsinām | sva-bhūmiḥ śvāpadādīnāṃ rājñāṃ sainyaṃ paraṃ balam
transliterated_devanagari: अम्भांसि जल-जन्तूनां दुर्गं दुर्ग-निवासिनाम् | स्व-भूमिः श्वापदादीनां राज्ञां सइन्यं परं बलम्
full_translation: The waters are a fortress for the creatures; the land is the own abode of the beasts and others, and the supreme strength of the kings is their army.

original_iast: upāyena hi yac chakyaṃ na tac chakyaṃ parākramaiḥ | kākī kanaka-sūtreṇa kṛṣṇa-sarpam aghātayat
transliterated_devanagari: उपायेन हि यच् छक्यं न तच् छक्यं पराक्रमइः | काकी कनक-सूत्रेण कृष्ण-सर्पम् अघातयत्
full_translation: Indeed, that which can be done by a method cannot be accomplished by valor; the crow struck the black snake with a golden thread.

original_iast: kulācāra-janācārair atiśuddhaḥ pratāpavān | dhārmiko nīti-kuśalaḥ sa svāmī yujyate bhuvi
transliterated_devanagari: कुलाचार-जनाचारइर् अतिशुद्धः प्रतापवान् | धार्मिको नीति-कुशलः स स्वामी युज्यते भुवि
full_translation: Indeed, he who is very pure, glorious, righteous, skilled in ethics, and a master is fit in this world according to family tradition and social conduct.

original_iast: aparaṃ ca paśya- rājānaṃ prathamaṃ vindet tato bhāryāṃ tato dhanam | rājany asati loke'smin kuto bhāryā kuto dhanam
transliterated_devanagari: अपरं च पश्य- राजानं प्रथमं विन्देत् ततो भार्यां ततो धनम् | राजन्य् असति लोकेऽस्मिन् कुतो भार्या कुतो धनम्
full_translation: "See, another king should first find a wife, then wealth. In this world of kshatriyas, where is a wife, and where is wealth?"

original_iast: anyac ca- parjanya iva bhūtānām ādhāraḥ pṛthivī-patiḥ | vikale'pi hi parjanye jīvyate na tu bhūpatau
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- पर्जन्य इव भूतानाम् आधारः पृथिवी-पतिः | विकलेऽपि हि पर्जन्ये जीव्यते न तु भूपतउ

word_by_word_translation.translation: by the lord of the earth

full_translation: And also, like rain is the support of beings, the earth is the lord; indeed, even when disturbed, it is sustained in rain, but not by the lord of the earth.

original_iast: niyata-viṣaya-vartī prāyaśo daṇḍa-yogāj jagati para-vaśe'smin durlabhaḥ sādhu-vṛtteḥ | kṛśam api vikalaṃ vā vyādhitaṃ vādhanaṃ vā patim api kula-nārī daṇḍa-bhītyābhyupaiti
transliterated_devanagari: नियत-विषय-वर्ती प्रायशो दण्ड-योगाज् जगति पर-वशेऽस्मिन् दुर्लभः साधु-वृत्तेः | कृशम् अपि विकलं वा व्याधितं वाधनं वा पतिम् अपि कुल-नारी दण्ड-भीत्याभ्युपइति
full_translation: In the world, generally, a fixed subject pertaining to punishment, under the control of this, is rarely found in the conduct of a virtuous person, even if they are thin, disabled, afflicted, or suffering, or even if they are a husband of a woman from a good family, approaches with fear of punishment.

original_iast: yadāsat-saṅga-rahito bhaviṣyasi bhaviṣyasi | yadāsajjana-goṣṭhīṣu patiṣyasi patiṣyasi
transliterated_devanagari: यदासत-सङ्ग-रहितो भविष्यसि भविष्यसि | यदासज्जन-गोष्ठीषु पतिष्यसि पतिष्यसि
full_translation: That which is present without attachment, you will be; that which is of the good people, you will fall in gatherings.

original_iast: ekasya duḥkhasya na yāvad antaṃ gacchāmy ahaṃ pāram ivārṇavasya | tāvad dvitīyaṃ samupasthitaṃ me chidreṣv anarthā bahulī-bhavanti
transliterated_devanagari: एकस्य दुःखस्य न यावद् अन्तं गच्छाम्य् अहं पारम् इवार्णवस्य | तावद् द्वितीयं समुपस्थितं मे छिद्रेष्व् अनर्था बहुली-भवन्ति
full_translation: I will not go until the end of one suffering; until I cross this ocean, many misfortunes arise in my holes.

original_iast: svabhāvajaṃ tu yan mitraṃ bhāgyenaivābhijāyate | tad-akṛtrima-sauhārdam āpatsv api na muñcati
transliterated_devanagari: स्वभावजं तु यन् मित्रं भाग्येनइवाभिजायते | तद-अकृत्रिम-सउहार्दम् आपत्स्व् अपि न मुञ्चति
full_translation: But that which is born of nature, a friend, is as if born by fortune; that unartificial goodwill does not abandon even in adversity.

original_iast: api ca- na mātari na dāreṣu na sodarye na cātmaje | viśvāsas tādṛśaḥ puṃsāṃ yādṛṅ mitre svabhāvaje
transliterated_devanagari: अपि च- न मातरि न दारेषु न सोदर्ये न चात्मजे | विश्वासस् तादृशः पुंसां यादृङ् मित्रे स्वभावजे
full_translation: Indeed, there is no trust in mothers, in wives, in brothers, or in sons among men of such nature as in friendship that is born of one's character.

original_iast: sva-karma-santāna-viceṣṭitāni kālāntarāvarti-śubhāśubhāni | ihaiva dṛṣṭāni mayaiva tāni janmāntarāṇīva daśāntarāṇi
transliterated_devanagari: स्व-कर्म-सन्तान-विचेष्टितानि कालान्तरावर्ति-शुभाशुभानि | इहइव दृष्टानि मयइव तानि जन्मान्तराणीव दशान्तराणि
full_translation: The actions of one's own descendants, performed over time, are seen here as auspicious and inauspicious, just as I perceive them; those are like the transformations of past lives.

original_iast: athavā ittham evaitat | kāyaḥ saṃnihitāpāyaḥ sampadaḥ padam āpadām | samāgamāḥ sāpagamāḥ sarvam utpādi bhaṅguram
transliterated_devanagari: अथवा इत्थम् एवइतत् | कायः संनिहितापायः सम्पदः पदम् आपदाम् | समागमाः सापगमाः सर्वम् उत्पादि भङ्गुरम्
full_translation: Or thus, indeed, this body, associated with danger, is a place of wealth amidst calamities, with all arrivals being fragile.

original_iast: punar vimṛśyāha- śokārāti-bhaya-trāṇaṃ prīti-viśrambha-bhājanam | kena ratnam idaṃ sṛṣṭaṃ mitram ity akṣara-dvayam
transliterated_devanagari: पुनर् विमृश्याह- शोकाराति-भय-त्राणं प्रीति-विश्रम्भ-भाजनम् | केन रत्नम् इदं सृष्टं मित्रम् इत्य् अक्षर-द्वयम्
full_translation: Again, having deliberated, the vessel of affection and trust provides protection from sorrow and fear. By whom has this gem, a friend, been created? Thus, it is a pair of letters.

original_iast: mitraṃ prīti-rasāyanaṃ nayanayor ānandanaṃ cetasaḥ pātraṃ yat sukha-duḥkhayoḥ samam idaṃ puṇyātmanā labhyate | ye cānye suhṛdaḥ samṛddhi-samaye dravyābhilāṣākulās te sarvatra milanti tattva-nikaṣa-grāvā tu teṣāṃ vipat
transliterated_devanagari: मित्रं प्रीति-रसायनं नयनयोर् आनन्दनं चेतसः पात्रं यत् सुख-दुःखयोः समम् इदं पुण्यात्मना लभ्यते | ये चान्ये सुहृदः समृद्धि-समये द्रव्याभिलाषाकुलास् ते सर्वत्र मिलन्ति तत्त्व-निकष-ग्रावा तु तेषां विपत्
full_translation: A friend is the elixir of affection, bringing joy to the eyes and serving as a vessel for the mind, which equally experiences happiness and sorrow. This is attained by the virtuous soul. Those who are other friends, desiring prosperity in time, meet everywhere, but the essence of truth is grasped only by them in times of misfortune.

original_iast: yo dhruvāṇi parityajya adhruvāṇi niṣevate | dhruvāṇi tasya naśyanti adhruvaṃ naṣṭam eva hi
transliterated_devanagari: यो ध्रुवाणि परित्यज्य अध्रुवाणि निषेवते | ध्रुवाणि तस्य नश्यन्ति अध्रुवं नष्टम् एव हि
full_translation: Who, abandoning the permanent things, enjoys the impermanent things, for that person, the permanent things are destroyed, and the impermanent things are indeed lost.

original_iast: mitraṃ yāntu ca sajjanā janapadair lakṣmīḥ samālabhyatāṃ bhūpālāḥ paripālayantu vasudhāṃ śaśvat sva-dharme sthitāḥ | āstāṃ mānasa-tuṣṭaye sukṛtināṃ nītir navoḍheva vaḥ kalyāṇaṃ kurutāṃ janasya bhagavāṃś candrārdha-cūḍāmaṇiḥ
transliterated_devanagari: मित्रं यान्तु च सज्जना जनपदइर् लक्ष्मीः समालभ्यतां भूपालाः परिपालयन्तु वसुधां शश्वत् स्व-धर्मे स्थिताः | आस्तां मानस-तुष्टये सुकृतिनां नीतिर् नवोढेव वः कल्याणं कुरुतां जनस्य भगवांश् चन्द्रार्ध-चूडामणिः
full_translation: May friends go forth, and may the good people attain prosperity through the citizens. May the kings always protect the earth, established in their own duties. May there be mental satisfaction for the virtuous, like a newly married woman. May you do welfare for the people, O divine one, the crest jewel of the half-moon.

original_iast: vardhamāno mahān sneho mṛgendra-vṛṣayor vane | piśunenātilubdhena jambukena vināśitaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: वर्धमानो महान् स्नेहो मृगेन्द्र-वृषयोर् वने | पिशुनेनातिलुब्धेन जम्बुकेन विनाशितः
full_translation: The great affection growing in the forest between the king of beasts (the lion) and the bulls was destroyed by the exceedingly greedy cunning jackal.

original_iast: adho 'dhaḥ paśyataḥ kasya mahimā nopacīyate | upary upari paśyantaḥ sarva eva daridrati
transliterated_devanagari: अधो ऽधः पश्यतः कस्य महिमा नोपचीयते | उपर्य् उपरि पश्यन्तः सर्व एव दरिद्रति
full_translation: "Indeed, all those who see above are in poverty; the greatness of whom is not attained by those who see below."

original_iast: aparaṃ ca- brahmahāpi naraḥ pūjyo yasyāsti vipulaṃ dhanam | śaśinas tulya-vaṃśo 'pi nirdhanaḥ paribhūyate
transliterated_devanagari: अपरं च- ब्रह्महापि नरः पूज्यो यस्यास्ति विपुलं धनम् | शशिनस् तुल्य-वंशो ऽपि निर्धनः परिभूयते
full_translation: Another man, even if he is a Brahmin and worthy of worship, whose wealth is abundant, is overshadowed by a lineage that is equal to that of the moon, even if it is poor.

original_iast: anyac ca- avyavasāyinam alasaṃ daiva-paraṃ sahasāc ca parihīṇam | pramadeva hi vṛddha-patiṃ necchaty avagūhituṃ lakṣmīḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- अव्यवसायिनम् अलसं दइव-परं सहसाच् च परिहीणम् | प्रमदेव हि वृद्ध-पतिं नेच्छत्य् अवगूहितुं लक्ष्मीः
full_translation: And also, the unambitious and lazy one, deprived of the divine and suddenly of the goddess of pleasure, indeed does not desire to embrace the old husband, Lakshmi.

original_iast: kiṃ ca- ālasyaṃ strī-sevā sa-rogatā janma-bhūmi-vātsalyam | santoṣo bhīrutvaṃ ṣaḍ vyāghātā mahattvasya
transliterated_devanagari: किं च- आलस्यं स्त्री-सेवा स-रोगता जन्म-भूमि-वात्सल्यम् | सन्तोषो भीरुत्वं षड् व्याघाता महत्त्वस्य
full_translation: What is more, laziness, service to women, sickness, birth, affection for the land, contentment, fearfulness, and the six tigers of importance.

original_iast: yataḥ- sampadā susthiraṃ-manyo bhavati svalpayāpi yaḥ | kṛtakṛtyo vidhir manye na vardhayati tasya tām
transliterated_devanagari: यतः- सम्पदा सुस्थिरं-मन्यो भवति स्वल्पयापि यः | कृतकृत्यो विधिर् मन्ये न वर्धयति तस्य ताम्
full_translation: From which prosperity becomes well-established in the mind, even a little, who having done actions does not increase the rule, I think, of him that.

original_iast: aparaṃ ca- nirutsāhaṃ nirānandaṃ nirvīryam ari-nandanam | mā sma sīmantinī kācij janayet putram īdṛśam
transliterated_devanagari: अपरं च- निरुत्साहं निरानन्दं निर्वीर्यम् अरि-नन्दनम् | मा स्म सीमन्तिनी काचिज् जनयेत् पुत्रम् ईदृशम्
full_translation: Do not give birth to a son of this kind, who is without enthusiasm, without joy, without strength, and is an enemy of Nanda.

original_iast: tathā coktam- alabdhaṃ caiva lipseta labdhaṃ rakṣet prayatnataḥ | rakṣitaṃ vardhayec caiva vṛddhaṃ pātreṣu nikṣipet
transliterated_devanagari: तथा चोक्तम- अलब्धं चइव लिप्सेत लब्धं रक्षेत् प्रयत्नतः | रक्षितं वर्धयेच् चइव वृद्धं पात्रेषु निक्षिपेत्
full_translation: Thus it is said: One should desire what is unobtained, protect what is obtained with effort, increase what is protected, and place what has grown in vessels.

original_iast: dhanena kiṃ yo na dadāti nāśnute balena kiṃ yaś ca ripūn na bādhate | śrutena kiṃ yo na ca dharmam ācaret kim ātmanā yo na jitendriyo bhavet
transliterated_devanagari: धनेन किं यो न ददाति नाश्नुते बलेन किं यश् च रिपून् न बाधते | श्रुतेन किं यो न च धर्मम् आचरेत् किम् आत्मना यो न जितेन्द्रियो भवेत्
full_translation: What use is wealth to one who does not give? What use is strength to one who does not overcome enemies? What use is knowledge to one who does not practice righteousness? What use is it for one who does not become a master of the senses?

original_iast: yataḥ, jala-bindu-nipātena kramaśaḥ pūryate ghaṭaḥ | sa hetuḥ sarva-vidyānāṃ dharmasya ca dhanasya ca
transliterated_devanagari: यतः, जल-बिन्दु-निपातेन क्रमशः पूर्यते घटः | स हेतुः सर्व-विद्यानां धर्मस्य च धनस्य च
full_translation: From which a drop of water, by its fall, gradually fills a pot; that is the cause of all knowledge, righteousness, and wealth.

original_iast: dānopabhoga-rahitā divasā yasya yānti vai | sa karma-kāra-bhastreva śvasann api na jīvati
transliterated_devanagari: दानोपभोग-रहिता दिवसा यस्य यान्ति वइ | स कर्म-कार-भस्त्रेव श्वसन्न् अपि न जीवति
full_translation: Indeed, the days devoid of charity and enjoyment, of which that action is the cause, do not live even like a breathing bellows.

original_iast: añjanasya kṣayaṃ dṛṣṭvā valmīkasya ca sañcayam | avandhyaṃ divasaṃ kuryād dānādhyayana-karmabhiḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अञ्जनस्य क्षयं दृष्ट्वा वल्मीकस्य च सञ्चयम् | अवन्ध्यं दिवसं कुर्याद् दानाध्ययन-कर्मभिः
full_translation: Having seen the destruction of the soot and the accumulation of the ant, one should unobstructedly perform the study of charity with actions during the day.

original_iast: yataḥ- ko 'tibhāraḥ samarthānāṃ kiṃ dūraṃ vyavasāyinām | ko videśaḥ savidyānāṃ kaḥ paraḥ priya-vādinām
transliterated_devanagari: यतः- को ऽतिभारः समर्थानां किं दूरं व्यवसायिनाम् | को विदेशः सविद्यानां कः परः प्रिय-वादिनाम्
full_translation: From where is the great burden of the capable? What is far for the industrious? Who is the foreign land for the learned? Who is the beloved other for the speakers?

original_iast: karotu nāma nīti-jño vyavasāyam itas tataḥ | phalaṃ punas tad eva syād yad vidher manasi sthitam
transliterated_devanagari: करोतु नाम नीति-ज्ञो व्यवसायम् इतस् ततः | फलं पुनस् तद् एव स्याद् यद् विधेर् मनसि स्थितम्
full_translation: Let one act according to the name of the policy, knowing the business; from here, then the result will indeed be whatever is established in the mind of the creator.

original_iast: kintu- vismayaḥ sarvathā heyaḥ pratyūhaḥ sarva-karmaṇām | tasmād vismayam utsṛjya sādhye siddhir vidhīyatām
transliterated_devanagari: किन्तु- विस्मयः सर्वथा हेयः प्रत्यूहः सर्व-कर्मणाम् | तस्माद् विस्मयम् उत्सृज्य साध्ये सिद्धिर् विधीयताम्
full_translation: However, wonder should always be avoided as a counteraction to all actions; therefore, giving up wonder, success should be established in the goal.

original_iast: nimagnasya payo-rāśau parvatāt patitasya ca | takṣakeṇāpi daṣṭasya āyur marmāṇi rakṣati
transliterated_devanagari: निमग्नस्य पयो-राशउ पर्वतात् पतितस्य च | तक्षकेणापि दष्टस्य आयुर् मर्माणि रक्षति
full_translation: The vital points of life are protected even when one is submerged in water, having fallen from the mountain, and bitten by the Takṣaka.

original_iast: nākāle miryate jantur viddhaḥ śara-śatair api | kuśāgreṇaiva saṃspṛṣṭaḥ prāpta-kālo na jīvati
transliterated_devanagari: नाकाले मिर्यते जन्तुर् विद्धः शर-शतइर् अपि | कुशाग्रेणइव संस्पृष्टः प्राप्त-कालो न जीवति
full_translation: In the time of death, the creature is killed, pierced by hundreds of arrows; even when touched by the tip of grass, having attained the time, it does not live.

original_iast: arakṣitaṃ tiṣṭhati daiva-rakṣitaṃ surakṣitaṃ daiva-hataṃ vinaśyati | jīvaty anātho 'pi vane visarjitaḥ kṛta-prayatno 'pi gṛhe na jīvati
transliterated_devanagari: अरक्षितं तिष्ठति दइव-रक्षितं सुरक्षितं दइव-हतं विनश्यति | जीवत्य् अनाथो ऽपि वने विसर्जितः कृत-प्रयत्नो ऽपि गृहे न जीवति
full_translation: An unprotected person stands; a divine being is protected and safeguarded. A divine being that is killed perishes, while an orphan, even if abandoned in the forest, does not live even after making an effort at home.

original_iast: nābhiṣeko na saṃskāraḥ siṃhasya kriyate mṛgaiḥ | vikramārjita-rājyasya svayam eva mṛgendratā
transliterated_devanagari: नाभिषेको न संस्कारः सिंहस्य क्रियते मृगइः | विक्रमार्जित-राज्यस्य स्वयम् एव मृगेन्द्रता

word_by_word_translation.translation: the quality of being a king of beasts

full_translation: There is no anointment or ritual performed for a lion that is acquired by the animals through valor; indeed, the quality of being a king of beasts is inherent.

original_iast: sevayā dhanam icchadbhiḥ sevakaiḥ paśya yat kṛtam | svātantryaṃ yac charīrasya mūḍhais tad api hāritam
transliterated_devanagari: सेवया धनम् इच्छद्भिः सेवकइः पश्य यत् कृतम् | स्वातन्त्र्यं यच् छरीरस्य मूढइस् तद् अपि हारितम्
full_translation: By the service desiring wealth, see what has been done: independence, which is also taken away by the foolish of the body.

original_iast: aparaṃ ca- śīta-vātātapa-kleśān sahante yān parāśritāḥ | tad-aṃśenāpi medhāvī tapas taptvā mukhī bhavet
transliterated_devanagari: अपरं च- शीत-वातातप-क्लेशान् सहन्ते यान् पराश्रिताः | तद-अंशेनापि मेधावी तपस् तप्त्वा मुखी भवेत्
full_translation: Those who take refuge endure the distresses of cold, wind, and sun; even a part of that austerity, having undergone it, makes one intelligent and becomes their face.

original_iast: anyac ca- etāvaj janmasāphalyaṃ dehinām iha dehiṣu | prāṇair arthair dhiyā vācā śreya evācaret sadā
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- एतावज् जन्मसाफल्यं देहिनाम् इह देहिषु | प्राणइर् अर्थइर् धिया वाचा श्रेय एवाचरेत् सदा
full_translation: And also, as much as the success of birth of embodied beings here in bodies should indeed be practiced by life forces, means, intellect, and speech, it is the best.

original_iast: aparaṃ ca- ehi gaccha patottiṣṭha vada maunaṃ samācara | iti vitrasta-sāraṅga-netrayā ko na vañcitaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अपरं च- एहि गच्छ पतोत्तिष्ठ वद मउनं समाचर | इति वित्रस्त-सारङ्ग-नेत्रया को न वञ्चितः
full_translation: "Come here, go, fall, rise, speak, maintain silence; thus, who is not deceived by the frightened deer with its eyes?"

original_iast: kiṃ ca- abudhair artha-lābhāya paṇya-strībhir iva svayam | ātmā saṃskṛtya saṃskṛtya paropakaraṇī-kṛtaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: किं च- अबुधइर् अर्थ-लाभाय पण्य-स्त्रीभिर् इव स्वयम् | आत्मा संस्कृत्य संस्कृत्य परोपकरणी-कृतः
full_translation: What is more, by the ignorant, the meaning for the benefit of goods, like women, the self, having been refined, is beneficially done.

original_iast: kiṃ ca- yā prakṛtyaiva capalā nipataty aśucāv api | svāmino bahu manyante dṛṣṭiṃ tām api sevakāḥ
transliterated_devanagari: किं च- या प्रकृत्यइव चपला निपतत्य् अशुचाव् अपि | स्वामिनो बहु मन्यन्ते दृष्टिं ताम् अपि सेवकाः
full_translation: What is more, the servants also think much of that vision, which is by nature fickle and falls into impurity, like the master.

original_iast: maunān mūrkhaḥ pravacana-paṭur bātulo jalpako vā kṣāntyā bhīrur yadi na sahate prāyaśo nābhijātaḥ | dhṛṣṭaḥ pārśve vasati niyataṃ dūrataś cāpragalbhaḥ sevā-dharmaḥ parama-gahano yoginām apy agamyaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: मउनान् मूर्खः प्रवचन-पटुर् बातुलो जल्पको वा क्षान्त्या भीरुर् यदि न सहते प्रायशो नाभिजातः | धृष्टः पार्श्वे वसति नियतं दूरतश् चाप्रगल्भः सेवा-धर्मः परम-गहनो योगिनाम् अप्य् अगम्यः
full_translation: A fool who is skilled in discourse, a madman who is talkative, or a timid person who cannot endure with patience, generally not of noble birth, is bold and dwells beside, constantly from afar, and is not very intelligent. The service of duty is supremely deep, even for the yogis, and is inaccessible.

original_iast: viśeṣataś ca- praṇamaty unnati-hetor jīvita-hetor vimuñcati prāṇān | duḥkhīyati sukha-hetoḥ ko mūḍhaḥ sevakād anyaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: विशेषतश् च- प्रणमत्य् उन्नति-हेतोर् जीवित-हेतोर् विमुञ्चति प्राणान् | दुःखीयति सुख-हेतोः को मूढः सेवकाद् अन्यः
full_translation: Especially, who is a fool that bows for the sake of progress, releases life for the sake of living, makes miserable for the sake of happiness, other than a servant?

original_iast: kathaṃ nāma na sevyante yatnataḥ parameśvarāḥ | acireṇaiva ye tuṣṭāḥ pūrayanti manorathān
transliterated_devanagari: कथं नाम न सेव्यन्ते यत्नतः परमेश्वराः | अचिरेणइव ये तुष्टाः पूरयन्ति मनोरथान्
full_translation: How are the Supreme Beings not served with effort, like those who, when satisfied, quickly fulfill desires?

original_iast: anyac ca- kutaḥ sevā-vihīnānāṃ cāmaroddhūta-sampadaḥ | uddaṇḍa-dhavala-cchatraṃ vāji-vāraṇa-vāhinī
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- कुतः सेवा-विहीनानां चामरोद्धूत-सम्पदः | उद्दण्ड-धवल-च्छत्रं वाजि-वारण-वाहिनी
full_translation: And also, from where is the service of those who are devoid of the wealth of the raised chamara, the unruly white umbrella carried by horses and elephants?

original_iast: avyāpareṣu vyāpāraṃ yo naraḥ kartum icchati | sa eva nidhanaṃ yāti kīlotpaṭīva vānaraḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अव्यापरेषु व्यापारं यो नरः कर्तुम् इच्छति | स एव निधनं याति कीलोत्पटीव वानरः
full_translation: A man who wishes to engage in non-transactional trade indeed goes to his death like a bolt, a monkey.

original_iast: parādhikāra-carcā yaḥ kuryāt svāmi-hitecchayā | sa viṣīdati cītkārād gardabhas tāḍito yathā
transliterated_devanagari: पराधिकार-चर्चा यः कुर्यात् स्वामि-हितेच्छया | स विषीदति चीत्काराद् गर्दभस् ताडितो यथा
full_translation: He who discusses the rights of others, with the intention of the master's welfare, becomes dejected, just like a donkey that has been struck from a cry.

original_iast: yataḥ- āśritānāṃ bhṛtau svāmi-sevāyāṃ dharma-sevane | putrasyotpādane caiva na santi pratihastakāḥ
transliterated_devanagari: यतः- आश्रितानां भृतउ स्वामि-सेवायां धर्म-सेवने | पुत्रस्योत्पादने चइव न सन्ति प्रतिहस्तकाः
full_translation: From those who are dependent in the service of the master, there are indeed no obstacles in serving righteousness, in the procreation of a son, and so forth.

original_iast: pṛṣṭhataḥ sevayed arkaṃ jaṭhareṇa hutāśanam | svāminaṃ sarva-bhāvena paralokam amāyayā
transliterated_devanagari: पृष्ठतः सेवयेद् अर्कं जठरेण हुताशनम् | स्वामिनं सर्व-भावेन परलोकम् अमायया
full_translation: One should serve the sun with the fire from the belly, the lord, with all feeling, without deceit regarding the afterlife.

original_iast: suhṛdām upakāra-kāraṇād dviṣatām apy apakāra-kāraṇāt | nṛpa-saṃśraya iṣyate budhair jaṭharaṃ ko na bibharti kevalam
transliterated_devanagari: सुहृदाम् उपकार-कारणाद् द्विषताम् अप्य् अपकार-कारणात् | नृप-संश्रय इष्यते बुधइर् जठरं को न बिभर्ति केवलम्
full_translation: The wise desire the shelter of a king, not due to the help of friends, even in the case of harm from enemies; who can bear only the belly?

original_iast: jīvite yasya jīvanti viprā mitrāṇi bāndhavāḥ | saphalaṃ jīvitaṃ tasya ātmārthe ko na jīvati
transliterated_devanagari: जीविते यस्य जीवन्ति विप्रा मित्राणि बान्धवाः | सफलं जीवितं तस्य आत्मार्थे को न जीवति

word_by_word_translation.translation: for the sake of the self

full_translation: In the life of one whose wise friends and relatives live, who does not live for the sake of the self?

original_iast: api ca- yasmin jīvati jīvanti bahavaḥ sa tu jīvatu | kāko 'pi kiṃ na kurute cañcvā svodara-pūraṇam
transliterated_devanagari: अपि च- यस्मिन् जीवति जीवन्ति बहवः स तु जीवतु | काको ऽपि किं न कुरुते चञ्च्वा स्वोदर-पूरणम्
full_translation: Indeed, in whom many live, he may live; but what does the crow do, even with a quick movement, to fill its own belly?

original_iast: paśya- pañcabhir yāti dāsatvaṃ purāṇaiḥ ko 'pi mānavaḥ | ko 'pi lakṣaiḥ kṛtī ko 'pi lakṣair api na labhyate
transliterated_devanagari: पश्य- पञ्चभिर् याति दासत्वं पुराणइः को ऽपि मानवः | को ऽपि लक्षइः कृती को ऽपि लक्षइर् अपि न लभ्यते
full_translation: Behold, by five, one attains servitude; who indeed is a human? Who indeed is an action by signs? Who indeed is even not obtained by signs?

original_iast: anyac ca- manuṣya-jātau tulyāyāṃ bhṛtyatvam ati-garhitam | prathamo yo na tan nāpi sa kiṃ jīvatsu gaṇyate
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- मनुष्य-जातउ तुल्यायां भृत्यत्वम् अति-गर्हितम् | प्रथमो यो न तन् नापि स किं जीवत्सु गण्यते
full_translation: And also, among humans, servitude that is equal is extremely blameworthy; the first who does not do that is not even considered among the living.

original_iast: tathā coktaṃ- vāji-vāraṇa-lohānāṃ kāṣṭha-pāṣāṇa-vāsasām | nārī-puruṣa-toyānām antaraṃ hada-hantaram
transliterated_devanagari: तथा चोक्तं- वाजि-वारण-लोहानां काष्ठ-पाषाण-वाससाम् | नारी-पुरुष-तोयानाम् अन्तरं हद-हन्तरम्
full_translation: Thus it is said, the essence of the garments of horses, elephants, iron, wood, stone, the woman, the man, and of water is to kill the killer.

original_iast: svalpa-snāyu-vasāvaśeṣa-malinaṃ nirmāṃsam apy asthikaṃ śvā labdhvā paritoṣam eti na bhavet tasya kṣudhaḥ śāntaye | siṃho jambukam aṅkam āgatam api tyaktvā nihanti dvipaṃ sarvaḥ kṛcchra-gato 'pi vāñchati janaḥ sattvānurūpaṃ phalam
transliterated_devanagari: स्वल्प-स्नायु-वसावशेष-मलिनं निर्मांसम् अप्य् अस्थिकं श्वा लब्ध्वा परितोषम् एति न भवेत् तस्य क्षुधः शान्तये | सिंहो जम्बुकम् अङ्कम् आगतम् अपि त्यक्त्वा निहन्ति द्विपं सर्वः कृच्छ्र-गतो ऽपि वाञ्छति जनः सत्त्वानुरूपं फलम्
full_translation: Even a dog, having obtained satisfaction from the remnants of a small, dirty body and even from bones, does not become free from hunger. For the peace of that hunger, a lion may kill a jackal that has come into its lap, yet even after abandoning it, it may still desire an elephant. All beings, having gone through difficulties, desire fruits according to their nature.

original_iast: lāṅgūla-cālanam adhaś caraṇāvapātaṃ bhūmau nipatya vadanodara-darśanaṃ ca | śvā piṇḍadasya kurute gaja-puṅgavas tu dhīraṃ vilokayati cāṭu-śataiś ca bhuṅkte
transliterated_devanagari: लाङ्गूल-चालनम् अधश् चरणावपातं भूमउ निपत्य वदनोदर-दर्शनं च | श्वा पिण्डदस्य कुरुते गज-पुङ्गवस् तु धीरं विलोकयति चाटु-शतइश् च भुङ्क्ते
full_translation: The tail moves downwards, and having fallen on the ground, the mouth and belly are visible. The dog does this with its body, but the best elephant observes wisely and eats the clever one among a hundred.

original_iast: yaj jīvyate kṣaṇam api prathitaṃ manuṣyair vijñāna-vikrama-yaśobhir abhajyamānam | tan nāma jīvitam iha pravadanti taj-jñāḥ kāko 'pi jīvati cirāya baliṃ ca bhuṅkte
transliterated_devanagari: यज् जीव्यते क्षणम् अपि प्रथितं मनुष्यइर् विज्ञान-विक्रम-यशोभिर् अभज्यमानम् | तन् नाम जीवितम् इह प्रवदन्ति तज-ज्ञाः काको ऽपि जीवति चिराय बलिं च भुङ्क्ते
full_translation: They say that life, which is lived even for a moment, is famous among humans for its knowledge, power, and glories, and should not be neglected. The wise ones say that even the crow lives for a long time and enjoys the offerings.

original_iast: yo nātmaje na ca gurau na ca bhṛtya-varge dīne dayāṃ na kurute na ca bandhu-varge | kiṃ tasya jīvita-phalena manuṣya-loke kāko 'pi jīvati cirāya baliṃ ca bhuṅkte
transliterated_devanagari: यो नात्मजे न च गुरउ न च भृत्य-वर्गे दीने दयां न कुरुते न च बन्धु-वर्गे | किं तस्य जीवित-फलेन मनुष्य-लोके काको ऽपि जीवति चिराय बलिं च भुङ्क्ते
full_translation: Who does not show compassion to those not born of oneself, nor to the teacher, nor to the servant, nor to the poor, nor to the relatives—what of his life in the world of man? Even a crow lives long and enjoys offerings.

original_iast: ahita-hita-vicāra-śūnya-buddheḥ śruti-samayair bahubhir bahiṣkṛtasya | udara-bharaṇa-mātra-kevalecchoḥ puruṣa-paśoś ca paśoś ca ko viśeṣaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अहित-हित-विचार-शून्य-बुद्धेः श्रुति-समयइर् बहुभिर् बहिष्कृतस्य | उदर-भरण-मात्र-केवलेच्छोः पुरुष-पशोश् च पशोश् च को विशेषः
full_translation: What is the distinction between a man and an animal, when the thoughts of unbeneficial and beneficial are empty in the intellect, when the hearing of time is excluded by many, and when the belly is filled only by mere desire?

original_iast: na kasyacit kaścid iha svabhāvād bhavaty udāro 'bhimataḥ khalo vā | loke gurutvaṃ viparītatāṃ vā sva-ceṣṭitāny eva naraṃ nayanti
transliterated_devanagari: न कस्यचित् कश्चिद् इह स्वभावाद् भवत्य् उदारो ऽभिमतः खलो वा | लोके गुरुत्वं विपरीततां वा स्व-चेष्टितान्य् एव नरं नयन्ति
full_translation: No one here becomes noble by nature, nor does anyone, by intention, become wicked; in the world, one's own actions indeed lead a man either to gravity or to its opposite.

original_iast: kiṃ ca- āropyate śilā śaile yatnena mahatā yathā | nipātyate kṣaṇenādhas tathātmā guṇa-doṣayoḥ
transliterated_devanagari: किं च- आरोप्यते शिला शइले यत्नेन महता यथा | निपात्यते क्षणेनाधस् तथात्मा गुण-दोषयोः
full_translation: What is placed on the mountain with great effort is dropped down in a moment; thus, the self is associated with qualities and faults.

original_iast: yāty adho 'dhaḥ vrajaty uccair naraḥ svair eva karmabhiḥ | kūpasya khanitā yadvat prākārasyeva kārakaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: यात्य् अधो ऽधः व्रजत्य् उच्चइर् नरः स्वइर् एव कर्मभिः | कूपस्य खनिता यद्वत् प्राकारस्येव कारकः
full_translation: A man indeed goes down, proceeds high, by his own actions, just as the cause of a dug well is like that of a wall.

original_iast: karaṭako brūte- udīrito 'rthaḥ paśunāpi gṛhyate hayāś ca nāgāś ca vahanti coditāḥ | anuktam apy ūhati paṇḍito janaḥ pareṅgita-jñāna-phalā hi buddhayaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: करटको ब्रूते- उदीरितो ऽर्थः पशुनापि गृह्यते हयाश् च नागाश् च वहन्ति चोदिताः | अनुक्तम् अप्य् ऊहति पण्डितो जनः परेङ्गित-ज्ञान-फला हि बुद्धयः
full_translation: The tortoise speaks; the meaning that has been raised is grasped even by animals. Horses and elephants carry when urged. Even if not spoken, the learned person conjectures. In another context, indeed, the fruits of knowledge are the intellects.

original_iast: ākāra-riṅgatair gatyā ceṣṭayā bhāṣaṇena ca | netra-vaktra-vikāreṇa lakṣyate'ntargataṃ manaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: आकार-रिङ्गतइर् गत्या चेष्टया भाषणेन च | नेत्र-वक्त्र-विकारेण लक्ष्यतेऽन्तर्गतं मनः
full_translation: The form is perceived through the movement, action, and speech, as well as by the transformation of the eyes and face, which reveals what is within the mind.

original_iast: prastāva-sadṛśaṃ vākyaṃ sad-bhāva-sadṛśaṃ priyam | ātma-śakti-samaṃ kopaṃ yo jānāti sa paṇḍitaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: प्रस्ताव-सदृशं वाक्यं सद-भाव-सदृशं प्रियम् | आत्म-शक्ति-समं कोपं यो जानाति स पण्डितः
full_translation: A wise person is one who knows a statement similar to a good emotion, a dear self, and equal power of anger.

original_iast: anāhūto viśed yas tu apṛṣṭo bahu bhāṣate | ātmānaṃ manyate prītaṃ bhū-pālasya sa durmatiḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अनाहूतो विशेद् यस् तु अपृष्टो बहु भाषते | आत्मानं मन्यते प्रीतं भू-पालस्य स दुर्मतिः
full_translation: He who enters uninvited and speaks much about himself, thinking himself to be pleased, is indeed of a bad intellect, the protector of the earth.

original_iast: kim apy asti svabhāvena sundaraṃ vāpy asundaram | yad eva rocate yasmai bhavet tat tasya sundaram
transliterated_devanagari: किम् अप्य् अस्ति स्वभावेन सुन्दरं वाप्य् असुन्दरम् | यद् एव रोचते यस्मइ भवेत् तत् तस्य सुन्दरम्
full_translation: What is, by nature, either beautiful or ugly, is indeed pleasing in that which it becomes; that is beautiful.

original_iast: yataḥ- yasya yasya hi yo bhāvas tena tena hi taṃ naram | anupraviśya medhāvī kṣipram ātma-vaśaṃ nayet
transliterated_devanagari: यतः- यस्य यस्य हि यो भावस् तेन तेन हि तं नरम् | अनुप्रविश्य मेधावी क्षिप्रम् आत्म-वशं नयेत्
full_translation: From whom, indeed, whose state is such, by him, indeed, that man, entering, the wise person quickly brings under control the self.

original_iast: anyac ca- ko 'trety aham iti brūyāt samyag ādeśayeti ca | ājñām avitathāṃ kuryād yathā-śakti mahīpateḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- को ऽत्रेत्य् अहम् इति ब्रूयात् सम्यग् आदेशयेति च | आज्ञाम् अवितथां कुर्याद् यथा-शक्ति महीपतेः
full_translation: "Moreover, who should speak here, thus I should properly give command, and the order should be performed as per the power of the king."

original_iast: aparaṃ ca- alpecchur dhṛtimān prājñaś chāyevānugataḥ sadā | ādiṣṭo na vikalpeta sa rāja-vasatiṃ vaset
transliterated_devanagari: अपरं च- अल्पेच्छुर् धृतिमान् प्राज्ञश् छायेवानुगतः सदा | आदिष्टो न विकल्पेत स राज-वसतिं वसेत्
full_translation: Another who desires little, being steadfast and wise, always following like a shadow, instructed not to choose, that king should reside in the dwelling.

original_iast: yataḥ- doṣa-bhīter anārambhas tat kāpuruṣa-lakṣaṇam | kair ajīrṇa-bhayād bhrātar bhojanaṃ parihīyate
transliterated_devanagari: यतः- दोष-भीतेर् अनारम्भस् तत् कापुरुष-लक्षणम् | कइर् अजीर्ण-भयाद् भ्रातर् भोजनं परिहीयते
full_translation: From which fear of fault arises, that is the characteristic of a coward; due to fear of indigestion, a brother avoids food.

original_iast: paśya- āsannam eva nṛpatir bhajate manuṣyaṃ vidyā-vihīnam akulīnam asaṃstutaṃ vā | prāyeṇa bhūmi-patayaḥ pramadā-latāś ca yaḥ pārśvato vasati taṃ pariveṣṭayanti
transliterated_devanagari: पश्य- आसन्नम् एव नृपतिर् भजते मनुष्यं विद्या-विहीनम् अकुलीनम् असंस्तुतं वा | प्रायेण भूमि-पतयः प्रमदा-लताश् च यः पार्श्वतो वसति तं परिवेष्टयन्ति
full_translation: Indeed, the king worships a man who is devoid of knowledge, of low birth, and not praised, or generally, the rulers of the earth and the beautiful women, as well as the creepers, surround him who dwells nearby.

original_iast: damanako brūte-śṛṇu- dūrād avekṣaṇaṃ hāsaḥ sampraśneṣv ādaro bhṛśam | parokṣe'pi guṇa-ślāghā smaraṇaṃ priya-vastuṣu
transliterated_devanagari: दमनको ब्रूते-शृणु- दूराद् अवेक्षणं हासः सम्प्रश्नेष्व् आदरो भृशम् | परोक्षेऽपि गुण-श्लाघा स्मरणं प्रिय-वस्तुषु
full_translation: Damanaka speaks: "Listen from afar, the observation is that laughter in inquiries is held in great respect. Even in the unseen, the remembrance of virtue and praise is dear in things."

original_iast: asevake cānuraktir dānaṃ sa-priya-bhāṣaṇam | anuraktasya cihnāni doṣe'pi guṇa-saṅgrahaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: असेवके चानुरक्तिर् दानं स-प्रिय-भाषणम् | अनुरक्तस्य चिह्नानि दोषेऽपि गुण-सङ्ग्रहः
full_translation: To the unserving, attachment is a beloved speech; for one who is attached, even in faults, there is a collection of virtues.

original_iast: anyac ca-- kāla-yāpanam āśānāṃ vardhanaṃ phala-khaṇḍanam | virakteśvara-cihnāni jānīyān matimān naraḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च-- काल-यापनम् आशानां वर्धनं फल-खण्डनम् | विरक्तेश्वर-चिह्नानि जानीयान् मतिमान् नरः
full_translation: A wise man should know the symbols of the detached lord, the extension of time, the increase of hopes, and the division of fruit.

original_iast: apāyasaṃ darśanajāṃ vipattim upāya-sandarśana-jāṃ ca siddhim | medhāvino nīti-vidhi-prayuktāṃ puraḥ sphurantīm iva darśayanti
transliterated_devanagari: अपायसं दर्शनजां विपत्तिम् उपाय-सन्दर्शन-जां च सिद्धिम् | मेधाविनो नीति-विधि-प्रयुक्तां पुरः स्फुरन्तीम् इव दर्शयन्ति
full_translation: They show, like a shining light before, the means of vision born from calamity and success, employed by the wise through policy and method.

original_iast: aprāpta-kālaṃ vacanaṃ bṛhaspatir api bruvan | labhate buddhy-avajñānam avamānaṃ ca bhārata
transliterated_devanagari: अप्राप्त-कालं वचनं बृहस्पतिर् अपि ब्रुवन् | लभते बुद्ध्य-अवज्ञानम् अवमानं च भारत
full_translation: Brihaspati, while speaking, also receives the word of the unattained time, along with intellect, ignorance, and disrespect, O Bharata.

original_iast: āpady unmārga-gamane kārya-kālātyayeṣu ca | apṛṣṭo 'pi hitānveṣī brūyāt kalyāṇa-bhāṣitam
transliterated_devanagari: आपद्य् उन्मार्ग-गमने कार्य-कालात्ययेषु च | अपृष्टो ऽपि हितान्वेषी ब्रूयात् कल्याण-भाषितम्
full_translation: In case of emergency, one should speak auspicious words, even if not asked, while on the right path in actions during times of urgency, as a seeker of welfare.

original_iast: kalpayati yena vṛttiṃ yena ca loke praśasyate | sa guṇas tena guṇinā rakṣyaḥ saṃvardhanīyaś ca
transliterated_devanagari: कल्पयति येन वृत्तिं येन च लोके प्रशस्यते | स गुणस् तेन गुणिना रक्ष्यः संवर्धनीयश् च
full_translation: He who creates a livelihood and is praised in the world, that quality should be protected and nurtured by him with qualities.

original_iast: dantasya nirgharṣaṇakena rājan karṇasya kaṇḍūyanakena vāpi | tṛṇena kāryaṃ bhavatīśvarāṇāṃ kim aṅga-vāk-pāṇi-matā nareṇa
transliterated_devanagari: दन्तस्य निर्घर्षणकेन राजन् कर्णस्य कण्डूयनकेन वापि | तृणेन कार्यं भवतीश्वराणां किम् अङ्ग-वाक-पाणि-मता नरेण

word_by_word_translation.translation: by the one who is causing pain

full_translation: O king, what work is to be done by the divine beings, whether by the pain caused to the tooth, or by the itching caused to the ear, or even by grass, as considered by a man in speech or action?

original_iast: kadarthitasyāpi ca dhairya-vṛtter buddher vināśo nahi śaṅkanīyaḥ | adhaḥ-kṛtasyāpi tanūnapāto nādhaḥ śikhā yāti kadācid eva
transliterated_devanagari: कदर्थितस्यापि च धइर्य-वृत्तेर् बुद्धेर् विनाशो नहि शङ्कनीयः | अधः-कृतस्यापि तनूनपातो नाधः शिखा याति कदाचिद् एव

word_by_word_translation.translation: even of one who has acted

full_translation: Even for one who is distressed, the destruction of patience and character should not be doubted; similarly, even for one who has acted, the fall of the body does not lead to a decline, as the flame sometimes does not go down.

original_iast: maṇir luṭhati pādeṣu kācaḥ śirasi dhāryate | yathaivāste tathaivāstāṃ kācaḥ kāco maṇir maṇiḥ
transliterated_devanagari: मणिर् लुठति पादेषु काचः शिरसि धार्यते | यथइवास्ते तथइवास्तां काचः काचो मणिर् मणिः
full_translation: A gem rolls on the feet, while glass is held on the head; just as it is, so it may be; glass, glass, a gem, a gem.

original_iast: anyac ca- nirviśeṣo yadā rājā samaṃ sarveṣu vartate | tadodyama-samarthānām utsāhaḥ parihīyate
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- निर्विशेषो यदा राजा समं सर्वेषु वर्तते | तदोद्यम-समर्थानाम् उत्साहः परिहीयते
full_translation: And also, when the king exists equally among all, then the enthusiasm of the capable is diminished.

original_iast: kiṃ ca- trividhāḥ puruṣā rājann uttamādhama-madhyamāḥ | niyojayet tathaivaitāṃs trividheṣv eva karmasu
transliterated_devanagari: किं च- त्रिविधाः पुरुषा राजन्न् उत्तमाधम-मध्यमाः | नियोजयेत् तथइवइतांस् त्रिविधेष्व् एव कर्मसु
full_translation: O king, what are the three kinds of men? The best, the worst, and the middle ones should indeed be assigned to these three kinds of actions.

original_iast: yataḥ- sthāna eva nijyojyante bhṛtyāś cābharaṇāni ca | nahi cūḍāmaṇiḥ pāde nūpuraṃ śirasā kṛtam
transliterated_devanagari: यतः- स्थान एव निज्योज्यन्ते भृत्याश् चाभरणानि च | नहि चूडामणिः पादे नूपुरं शिरसा कृतम्
full_translation: Indeed, from that place, the ornaments of the servants are to be used, and not the crown jewel made for the head, nor the anklets for the feet.

original_iast: api ca- kanaka-bhūṣaṇa-saṅgrahaṇocito yadi maṇis trapuṇi praṇidhīyate | na sa virauti na cāpi na śobhate bhavati yojayitur vacanīyatā
transliterated_devanagari: अपि च- कनक-भूषण-सङ्ग्रहणोचितो यदि मणिस् त्रपुणि प्रणिधीयते | न स विरउति न चापि न शोभते भवति योजयितुर् वचनीयता
full_translation: Also, if a gem is offered appropriately for gathering gold ornaments, he does not shine, nor is he beautiful; thus, the quality of being spoken of the one who joins becomes diminished.

original_iast: anyac ca- mukuṭe ropitā kācaś caraṇābharaṇe maṇiḥ | nahi doṣo maṇer asti kintu sādhor avijñatā
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- मुकुटे रोपिता काचश् चरणाभरणे मणिः | नहि दोषो मणेर् अस्ति किन्तु साधोर् अविज्ञता
full_translation: Also, in the crown, a glass gem is planted in the foot ornaments; there is no fault of the gem, but it is the ignorance of the good person.

original_iast: paśya- buddhimān anurakto 'yam ayaṃ śūra ito bhayam | iti bhṛtya-vicārajño bhṛtyair āpūryate nṛpaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: पश्य- बुद्धिमान् अनुरक्तो ऽयम् अयं शूर इतो भयम् | इति भृत्य-विचारज्ञो भृत्यइर् आपूर्यते नृपः
full_translation: "Behold, this wise one is attached; this brave one, from here, is fearsome. Thus, the knowledgeable servant is filled by the servants, O king."

original_iast: tathā hi- aśvaḥ śastraṃ śāstraṃ vīṇā vāṇī naraś ca nārī ca | puruṣa-viśeṣaṃ prāptā bhavanty ayogyāś ca yogyāś ca
transliterated_devanagari: तथा हि- अश्वः शस्त्रं शास्त्रं वीणा वाणी नरश् च नारी च | पुरुष-विशेषं प्राप्ता भवन्त्य् अयोग्याश् च योग्याश् च
full_translation: Thus, indeed, the horse, the weapon, the scripture, the veena, speech, man, and woman, as well as the special man, become both unworthy and worthy.

original_iast: anyac ca- kiṃ bhaktenāsamarthena kiṃ śaktenāpakāriṇā | bhaktaṃ śaktaṃ ca māṃ rājan nāvajñātuṃ tvam arhasi
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- किं भक्तेनासमर्थेन किं शक्तेनापकारिणा | भक्तं शक्तं च मां राजन् नावज्ञातुं त्वम् अर्हसि
full_translation: And also, what can a devotee who is incapable do? What can a capable one who is harmful do? O king, you are not worthy to disregard me.

original_iast: avajñānād rājño bhavati mati-hīnaḥ parijanas tatas tat-prāmāṇyād bhavati na samīpe budha-janaḥ | budhais tyakte rājye na hi bhavati nītir guṇavatī vipannāyāṃ nītau sakalam avaśaṃ sīdati jagat
transliterated_devanagari: अवज्ञानाद् राज्ञो भवति मति-हीनः परिजनस् ततस् तत-प्रामाण्याद् भवति न समीपे बुध-जनः | बुधइस् त्यक्ते राज्ये न हि भवति नीतिर् गुणवती विपन्नायां नीतउ सकलम् अवशं सीदति जगत्
full_translation: From ignorance, the king's intellect becomes devoid of subjects; thereafter, from that authority, there is no wise person near. When the wise are abandoned in the kingdom, indeed, law does not become virtuous, and all aspects of the law sit helpless in a state of downfall in the world.

original_iast: aparaṃ ca- janaṃ janapadā nityam arcayanti nṛpārcitam | nṛpeṇāvamato yas tu sa sarvair avamanyate
transliterated_devanagari: अपरं च- जनं जनपदा नित्यम् अर्चयन्ति नृपार्चितम् | नृपेणावमतो यस् तु स सर्वइर् अवमन्यते
full_translation: Another group of people always worship the king's worship, but he who is disregarded by the king is disrespected by all.

original_iast: kiṃ ca- bālād api gṛhītavyaṃ yuktam uktaṃ manīṣibhiḥ | raver aviṣaye kiṃ na pradīpasya prakāśanam
transliterated_devanagari: किं च- बालाद् अपि गृहीतव्यं युक्तम् उक्तं मनीषिभिः | रवेर् अविषये किं न प्रदीपस्य प्रकाशनम्
full_translation: What, then, should also be taken from a child? It has been said by the wise that in the matter of the sun, what is not the illumination of a lamp?

original_iast: bandhu-strī-bhṛtya-vargasya buddheḥ sattvasya cātmanaḥ | āpan-nikaṣa-pāṣāṇe naro jānāti sāratām
transliterated_devanagari: बन्धु-स्त्री-भृत्य-वर्गस्य बुद्धेः सत्त्वस्य चात्मनः | आपन-निकष-पाषाणे नरो जानाति सारताम्
full_translation: A man knows the essence of the highest standard in stone, of the intellect of the class of women, of the servant, and of the essence of the self.

original_iast: yasya prasāde padmāste vijayaś ca parākrame | mṛtyuś ca vasati krodhe sarva-tejomayo hi saḥ
transliterated_devanagari: यस्य प्रसादे पद्मास्ते विजयश् च पराक्रमे | मृत्युश् च वसति क्रोधे सर्व-तेजोमयो हि सः
full_translation: "Whose grace, the lotuses, victory, and valor dwell in anger; indeed, he is all-radiant."

original_iast: tathā hi- bālo 'pi nāvamantavyo manuṣya iti bhūmipaḥ | mahatī devatā hy eṣā nara-rūpeṇa tiṣṭhati
transliterated_devanagari: तथा हि- बालो ऽपि नावमन्तव्यो मनुष्य इति भूमिपः | महती देवता ह्य् एषा नर-रूपेण तिष्ठति
full_translation: Thus, indeed, even a child should not be underestimated; indeed, this great deity, the king, stands in the form of a man.

original_iast: nirapekṣo na kartavyo bhṛtyai svāmī kadācana | nirapekṣaṃ prabhuṃ kṛtvā bhṛtyaḥ syād dadhi-karṇavat
transliterated_devanagari: निरपेक्षो न कर्तव्यो भृत्यइ स्वामी कदाचन | निरपेक्षं प्रभुं कृत्वा भृत्यः स्याद् दधि-कर्णवत्
full_translation: A servant should never act independently; having made the lord independent, the servant should be like the ear.

original_iast: kṣudra-śatrur bhaved yas tu vikramān naiva labhyate | tam āhantuṃ puraskāryaḥ sadṛśas tasya sainikaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: क्षुद्र-शत्रुर् भवेद् यस् तु विक्रमान् नइव लभ्यते | तम् आहन्तुं पुरस्कार्यः सदृशस् तस्य सइनिकः
full_translation: A small enemy may become one who is valiant, but he who is not obtained is worthy of reward to defeat; similar is the soldier of him.

original_iast: ājñā-bhaṅgo narendrāṇāṃ brāhmaṇānām anādaraḥ | pṛthak śayyā ca nārīṇām aśastra-vihito vadhaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: आज्ञा-भङ्गो नरेन्द्राणां ब्राह्मणानाम् अनादरः | पृथक् शय्या च नारीणाम् अशस्त्र-विहितो वधः
full_translation: The command to break the disrespect towards kings and Brahmins, the separate bed for women, and the prescribed killing of the unarmed.

original_iast: matir eva balād garīyasī yad-abhāve kariṇām iyaṃ daśā | iti ghoṣayatīva ḍiṇḍimaḥ kariṇo hastipakāhataḥ kvaṇan
transliterated_devanagari: मतिर् एव बलाद् गरीयसी यद-अभावे करिणाम् इयं दशा | इति घोषयतीव डिण्डिमः करिणो हस्तिपकाहतः क्वणन्
full_translation: Indeed, the mind, by force, is greater; in the absence of elephants, this condition thus proclaims, as if the drum of the elephants resounds when struck by an elephant.

original_iast: prativācam adatta keśavaḥ śapamānāya na cedi-bhūbhuje | anuhuṅkurute ghana-dhvaniṃ na hi gomāyu-rutāni kesarī
transliterated_devanagari: प्रतिवाचम् अदत्त केशवः शपमानाय न चेदि-भूभुजे | अनुहुङ्कुरुते घन-ध्वनिं न हि गोमायु-रुतानि केसरी
full_translation: Keshava did not give a response for the sake of cursing; if he does not cause the dense sound to tremble, indeed, the sounds of the cow-like lion do not arise.

original_iast: tṛṇāni nonmūlayati prabhañjano mṛdūni nīcaiḥ praṇalāni sarvataḥ | samucchritān eva tarūn prabādhate mahān mahaty eva karoti vikramam
transliterated_devanagari: तृणानि नोन्मूलयति प्रभञ्जनो मृदूनि नीचइः प्रणलानि सर्वतः | समुच्छ्रितान् एव तरून् प्रबाधते महान् महत्य् एव करोति विक्रमम्
full_translation: The one who breaks does not uproot the soft grasses; indeed, from all sides, the lowly streams raise the young ones and afflict the great, indeed performing a valiant deed.

original_iast: śabda-mātrān na bhetavyam ajñātvā śabda-kāraṇam | śabda-hetuṃ parijñāya kuṭṭanī gauravaṃ gatā
transliterated_devanagari: शब्द-मात्रान् न भेतव्यम् अज्ञात्वा शब्द-कारणम् | शब्द-हेतुं परिज्ञाय कुट्टनी गउरवं गता
full_translation: One should not fear the quantities of words, not knowing the cause of the word; understanding the reason for the word, the weight of the hammer has gone.

original_iast: nānivedya prakurvīta bhartuḥ kiṃcid api svayam | kāryam āpat-pratīkārād anyatra jagatī-pate
transliterated_devanagari: नानिवेद्य प्रकुर्वीत भर्तुः किंचिद् अपि स्वयम् | कार्यम् आपत-प्रतीकाराद् अन्यत्र जगती-पते
full_translation: One should not act without informing the lord; one should do anything by oneself in case of an emergency, rather than relying on the remedy from elsewhere in the world.

original_iast: anyac ca- kamaṇḍalūpamo 'mātyas tanu-tyāgī bahu-grahaḥ | nṛpate kiṅkṣaṇo mūrkho daridraḥ kiṃvarāṭakaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- कमण्डलूपमो ऽमात्यस् तनु-त्यागी बहु-ग्रहः | नृपते किङ्क्षणो मूर्खो दरिद्रः किंवराटकः
full_translation: Also, the minister, thin and a renouncer, has many houses; he is of little worth, foolish, poor, and from Kinvārāṭaka.

original_iast: sa hy amātyaḥ sadā śreyān kākinīṃ yaḥ pravardhayet | koṣaḥ koṣavataḥ prāṇāḥ prāṇāḥ prāṇā na bhūpateḥ
transliterated_devanagari: स ह्य् अमात्यः सदा श्रेयान् काकिनीं यः प्रवर्धयेत् | कोषः कोषवतः प्राणाः प्राणाः प्राणा न भूपतेः
full_translation: Indeed, he who always nurtures the crow is better than the one whose life is not that of the king's treasure.

original_iast: kiṃ cārthair na kulācāraiḥ sevatām eti pūruṣaḥ | dhana-hīnaḥ sva-patnyāpi tyajyate kiṃ punaḥ paraiḥ
transliterated_devanagari: किं चार्थइर् न कुलाचारइः सेवताम् एति पूरुषः | धन-हीनः स्व-पत्न्यापि त्यज्यते किं पुनः परइः
full_translation: What use is wealth if a man, devoid of it, is not served by family traditions? Even his own wife is abandoned; what then can be expected from others?

original_iast: ativyayo 'napekṣā ca tathārjanam adharmataḥ | moṣaṇaṃ dūra-saṃsthānāṃ koṣa-vyasanam ucyate
transliterated_devanagari: अतिव्ययो ऽनपेक्षा च तथार्जनम् अधर्मतः | मोषणं दूर-संस्थानां कोष-व्यसनम् उच्यते
full_translation: Excessive expenditure without consideration, along with earning unrightfully, leads to the destruction of far-off establishments and is said to be an addiction to treasure.

original_iast: yataḥ- kṣipram āyatam anālocya vyayamānaḥ sva-vāñchayā | parikṣīyata evāsau dhanī vaiśravaṇopamaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: यतः- क्षिप्रम् आयतम् अनालोच्य व्ययमानः स्व-वाञ्छया | परिक्षीयत एवासउ धनी वइश्रवणोपमः
full_translation: Indeed, he who is wealthy, like Vaishravana, is tested by his own desires, without consideration, quickly to be attained while spending.

original_iast: brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo bandhur nādhikāre praśasyate | brāhmaṇaḥ siddham apy arthaṃ kṛcchreṇāpi na yacchati
transliterated_devanagari: ब्राह्मणः क्षत्रियो बन्धुर् नाधिकारे प्रशस्यते | ब्राह्मणः सिद्धम् अप्य् अर्थं कृच्छ्रेणापि न यच्छति
full_translation: A Brahmin and a Kshatriya, though related, are not praised in authority; even an accomplished Brahmin does not give wealth, even with difficulty.

original_iast: niyuktaḥ kṣatriyo dravye khaḍgaṃ darśayate dhruvam | sarvasvaṃ grasate bandhur ākramya jñāti-bhāvataḥ
transliterated_devanagari: नियुक्तः क्षत्रियो द्रव्ये खड्गं दर्शयते ध्रुवम् | सर्वस्वं ग्रसते बन्धुर् आक्रम्य ज्ञाति-भावतः
full_translation: The appointed warrior certainly shows the sword in wealth, devours everything, attacking the relative, and knows the emotional state.

original_iast: aparādhe'pi niḥśaṅko niyogī cira-sevakaḥ | sa svāminam avajñāya carec ca niravagrahaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अपराधेऽपि निःशङ्को नियोगी चिर-सेवकः | स स्वामिनम् अवज्ञाय चरेच् च निरवग्रहः
full_translation: Even in the case of an offense, the appointed servant, without doubt, disregarding the master, acts without hesitation.

original_iast: upakartādhikāra-sthaḥ svāparādhaṃ na manyate | upakāraṃ dhvajī-kṛtya sarvam eva vilumpati
transliterated_devanagari: उपकर्ताधिकार-स्थः स्वापराधं न मन्यते | उपकारं ध्वजी-कृत्य सर्वम् एव विलुम्पति
full_translation: The authority to help, when established, does not consider one's own offense; indeed, the flag's action destroys all.

original_iast: upaṃśu-krīḍito 'mātyaḥ svayaṃ rājāyate yataḥ | avajñā kriyate tena sadā paricayād dhruvam
transliterated_devanagari: उपंशु-क्रीडितो ऽमात्यः स्वयं राजायते यतः | अवज्ञा क्रियते तेन सदा परिचयाद् ध्रुवम्
full_translation: The minister, who is played in the shadow, is honored by the king because disrespect is done; therefore, certainly, he is always acquainted.

original_iast: antar-duṣṭaḥ kṣamā-yuktaḥ sarvānartha-karaḥ kila | śakuniḥ śakaṭāraś ca dṛṣṭāntāv atra bhūpate
transliterated_devanagari: अन्तर-दुष्टः क्षमा-युक्तः सर्वानर्थ-करः किल | शकुनिः शकटारश् च दृष्टान्ताव् अत्र भूपते
full_translation: Indeed, within the wicked, forgiveness is endowed; the doer of all mischief is like the bird and the cart driver, as seen in examples here, O king.

original_iast: sadāmatyo na sādhyaḥ syāt samṛddhaḥ sarva eva hi | siddhānām ayam ādeśaḥ ṛddhiś citta-vikāriṇī
transliterated_devanagari: सदामत्यो न साध्यः स्यात् समृद्धः सर्व एव हि | सिद्धानाम् अयम् आदेशः ऋद्धिश् चित्त-विकारिणी
full_translation: This instruction is certainly not achievable for an always prosperous minister; it transforms the mind towards prosperity.

original_iast: prāptārtha-grahaṇaṃ dravya-parīvarto 'nurodhanam | upekṣā buddhi-hīnatvaṃ bhogo 'mātyasya dūṣaṇam
transliterated_devanagari: प्राप्तार्थ-ग्रहणं द्रव्य-परीवर्तो ऽनुरोधनम् | उपेक्षा बुद्धि-हीनत्वं भोगो ऽमात्यस्य दूषणम्
full_translation: The acceptance of an attained goal is a transformation of substance; persuasion is neglect. A deficiency in intellect leads to the enjoyment of the minister's corruption.

original_iast: niyogy artha-grahopāyo rājñā nitya-parīkṣaṇam | pratipatti-pradānaṃ ca tathā karma-viparyayaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: नियोग्य् अर्थ-ग्रहोपायो राज्ञा नित्य-परीक्षणम् | प्रतिपत्ति-प्रदानं च तथा कर्म-विपर्ययः
full_translation: The appropriate means of acquisition, constant examination by the king, provision of acquisition, and also the reversal of actions.

original_iast: nipīḍitā vamanty uccair antaḥ-sāraṃ mahīpateḥ | duṣṭa-vraṇā iva prāyo bhavanti hi niyoginaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: निपीडिता वमन्त्य् उच्चइर् अन्तः-सारं महीपतेः | दुष्ट-व्रणा इव प्रायो भवन्ति हि नियोगिनः
full_translation: Indeed, those who are engaged become like the wicked wounds of the king, vomiting loudly from the essence inside, when oppressed.

original_iast: muhur niyoginī bādhyā vasudhārā mahīpate | sakṛt kiṃ pīḍitaṃ snāna-vastraṃ muñced dhṛtaṃ payaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: मुहुर् नियोगिनी बाध्या वसुधारा महीपते | सकृत् किं पीडितं स्नान-वस्त्रं मुञ्चेद् धृतं पयः
full_translation: O lord of the earth, the appointed one is often afflicted. What should be released once is the bathing cloth held in milk?

original_iast: ājñā-bhaṅga-karān rājā na kṣameta sutān api | viśeṣaḥ ko nu rājñaś ca rājñaś citra-gatasya ca
transliterated_devanagari: आज्ञा-भङ्ग-करान् राजा न क्षमेत सुतान् अपि | विशेषः को नु राज्ञश् च राज्ञश् चित्र-गतस्य च
full_translation: The king, who breaks commands, cannot tolerate even his sons; who indeed can withstand the king, especially when he is in a state of distraction?

original_iast: stabdhasya naśyati yaśo viṣam asya maitrī naṣṭendriyasya kulam artha-parasya dharmaḥ | vidyā-phalaṃ vyasaninaḥ kṛpaṇasya saukhyaṃ rājyaṃ pramatta-sacivasya narādhipasya
transliterated_devanagari: स्तब्धस्य नश्यति यशो विषम् अस्य मइत्री नष्टेन्द्रियस्य कुलम् अर्थ-परस्य धर्मः | विद्या-फलं व्यसनिनः कृपणस्य सउख्यं राज्यं प्रमत्त-सचिवस्य नराधिपस्य

word_by_word_translation.translation: of the one who has lost his senses

full_translation: The fame of the stunned perishes like poison; the friendship of one who has lost his senses destroys the family. The wealth of another is the duty; knowledge bears fruit for the afflicted. The happiness of the miser is the kingdom of the careless minister, the king of men.

original_iast: aparaṃ ca- taskarebhyo niyuktebhyaḥ śatrubhyo nṛpa-vallabhāt | nṛpatir nija-lobhāc ca prajā rakṣet piteva hi
transliterated_devanagari: अपरं च- तस्करेभ्यो नियुक्तेभ्यः शत्रुभ्यो नृप-वल्लभात् | नृपतिर् निज-लोभाच् च प्रजा रक्षेत् पितेव हि
full_translation: O king, one should protect the subjects from appointed thieves and enemies, indeed, like a father, from one's own greed.

original_iast: svarṇa-rekhām ahaṃ spṛṣṭvā baddhvātmānaṃ ca dūtikā | āditsuś ca maṇiṃ sādhuḥ sva-doṣād duḥkhitā ime
transliterated_devanagari: स्वर्ण-रेखाम् अहं स्पृष्ट्वा बद्ध्वात्मानं च दूतिका | आदित्सुश् च मणिं साधुः स्व-दोषाद् दुःखिता इमे
full_translation: Having touched the golden line and having bound the self, the messenger, in the beginning, the good person with the gem, is distressed from his own fault.

original_iast: rajanī-cara-nāthena khaṇḍite timire niśi | yūnāṃ manāṃsi vivyādha dṛṣṭvā dṛṣṭvā manobhavaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: रजनी-चर-नाथेन खण्डिते तिमिरे निशि | यूनां मनांसि विव्याध दृष्ट्वा दृष्ट्वा मनोभवः
full_translation: In the night, the moving lord pierced the minds of the youth, having seen the broken darkness, having seen it again, he became mind-born.

original_iast: āditya-candrāvanilānalaś ca dyaur bhūmir āpo hṛdayaṃ yamaś ca | ahaś ca rātriś ca ubhe ca sandhye dharmaś ca jānāti narasya vṛttam
transliterated_devanagari: आदित्य-चन्द्रावनिलानलश् च द्यउर् भूमिर् आपो हृदयं यमश् च | अहश् च रात्रिश् च उभे च सन्ध्ये धर्मश् च जानाति नरस्य वृत्तम्
full_translation: Aditya, the moon, the blue fire, the sky, the earth, the waters, the heart, Yama, the day, the night, both twilights, and Dharma all know the conduct of a man.

original_iast: atathyāny api tathyāni darśayanti hi peśalāḥ | same nimnonnatānīva citra-karma-vido janāḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अतथ्यान्य् अपि तथ्यानि दर्शयन्ति हि पेशलाः | समे निम्नोन्नतानीव चित्र-कर्म-विदो जनाः

word_by_word_translation.translation: like the low and the high

full_translation: Indeed, skilled individuals show both other truths and truths equally, like the varied actions of knowledgeable people, whether they are low or high.

original_iast: utpanneṣu ca kāryeṣu matir yasya na hīyate | sa nistarati durgāṇi gopī jāra-dvayaṃ yathā
transliterated_devanagari: उत्पन्नेषु च कार्येषु मतिर् यस्य न हीयते | स निस्तरति दुर्गाणि गोपी जार-द्वयं यथा
full_translation: He who does not let his intellect be diminished in the arising tasks, he crosses over difficult situations like an old cowherd.

original_iast: nāgnis tṛpyati kāṣṭhānāṃ nāpagānāṃ mahodadhiḥ | nāntakaḥ sarva-bhūtānāṃ na puṃsāṃ vāma-locanā
transliterated_devanagari: नाग्निस् तृप्यति काष्ठानां नापगानां महोदधिः | नान्तकः सर्व-भूतानां न पुंसां वाम-लोचना
full_translation: The fire is satisfied by the wood, the great ocean is not the end for all beings, nor is it for men with the left eye.

original_iast: na dānena na mānena nārjavena na sevayā | na śastreṇa na śāstreṇa sarvathā viṣamāḥ striyaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: न दानेन न मानेन नार्जवेन न सेवया | न शस्त्रेण न शास्त्रेण सर्वथा विषमाः स्त्रियः
full_translation: Women are difficult in all respects, whether by donation, honor, straightforwardness, service, weapon, or scripture.

original_iast: guṇāśrayaṃ kīrti-yutaṃ ca kāntaṃ patiṃ ratijñaṃ sadhanaṃ yuvānam | vihāya śīghraṃ vanitā vrajanti narāntaraṃ śīla-guṇādi-hīnam
transliterated_devanagari: गुणाश्रयं कीर्ति-युतं च कान्तं पतिं रतिज्ञं सधनं युवानम् | विहाय शीघ्रं वनिता व्रजन्ति नरान्तरं शील-गुणादि-हीनम्
full_translation: Quickly leaving, a woman goes to a man who is handsome, youthful, wealthy, and knowledgeable in love, but lacking in character and other qualities.

original_iast: na tādṛśīṃ prītim upaiti nārī vicitra-śayyā śayitāpi kāmam | yathā hi dūrvādi-vikīrṇa-bhūmau prayāti saukhyaṃ para-kānti-saṅgāt
transliterated_devanagari: न तादृशीं प्रीतिम् उपइति नारी विचित्र-शय्या शयितापि कामम् | यथा हि दूर्वादि-विकीर्ण-भूमउ प्रयाति सउख्यं पर-कान्ति-सङ्गात्
full_translation: A woman does not approach such affection, even when lying on a strange bed, just as scattered grass goes across the earth, indeed with happiness from the association of another beloved.

original_iast: āhāro dviguṇaḥ strīṇāṃ buddhis tāsāṃ catur-guṇā | ṣaḍ-guṇo vyavasāyaś ca kāmāś cāṣṭaguṇaḥ smṛtaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: आहारो द्विगुणः स्त्रीणां बुद्धिस् तासां चतुर-गुणा | षड-गुणो व्यवसायश् च कामाश् चाष्टगुणः स्मृतः
full_translation: The food of women is double; their intellect has four qualities, six qualities in their profession, and their desires are remembered as eightfold.

original_iast: upāyena jayo yādṛg ripos tādṛṅ na hetibhiḥ | upāya-jño 'lpa-kāyo 'pi na śūraiḥ paribhūyate
transliterated_devanagari: उपायेन जयो यादृग् रिपोस् तादृङ् न हेतिभिः | उपाय-ज्ञो ऽल्प-कायो ऽपि न शूरइः परिभूयते
full_translation: Victory over the enemy of whatever kind is not achieved merely by reasons; even a small body is not overwhelmed by the brave through strategy.

original_iast: duṣṭā bhāryā śaṭhaṃ mitraṃ bhṛtyaś cottara-dāyakaḥ | sa-sarpe ca gṛhe vāso mṛtyur eva na saṃśayaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: दुष्टा भार्या शठं मित्रं भृत्यश् चोत्तर-दायकः | स-सर्पे च गृहे वासो मृत्युर् एव न संशयः
full_translation: Indeed, there is no doubt that a wicked wife, a deceitful friend, and a servant who gives answers are like a snake dwelling in the house.

original_iast: buddhir yasya balaṃ tasya nirbuddhes tu kuto balam | paśya siṃho madonmattaḥ śaśakena nipātitaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: बुद्धिर् यस्य बलं तस्य निर्बुद्धेस् तु कुतो बलम् | पश्य सिंहो मदोन्मत्तः शशकेन निपातितः
full_translation: The intellect of one who possesses strength is indeed unmatched among the foolish; but from where can strength come? Behold, even an intoxicated lion can be struck down by a hare.

original_iast: trāsa-hetor vinītis tu kriyate jīvitāśayā | pañcatvaṃ ced gamiṣyāmi kiṃ siṃhānunayena me
transliterated_devanagari: त्रास-हेतोर् विनीतिस् तु क्रियते जीविताशया | पञ्चत्वं चेद् गमिष्यामि किं सिंहानुनयेन मे

word_by_word_translation.translation: by the persuasion of a lion

full_translation: But humility is practiced out of fear of the cause; if I intend to live in a fivefold state, what will I gain by the persuasion of a lion?

original_iast: āpady unmārga-gamane kārya-kālātyayeṣu ca | kalyāṇa-vacanaṃ brūyād apṛṣṭo 'pi hito naraḥ
transliterated_devanagari: आपद्य् उन्मार्ग-गमने कार्य-कालात्ययेषु च | कल्याण-वचनं ब्रूयाद् अपृष्टो ऽपि हितो नरः
full_translation: In case of an emergency, a man should speak auspicious words while on the right path in matters of time, even if he is not asked, as it is beneficial.

original_iast: anyac ca- bhogasya bhājanaṃ rājā na rājā kārya-bhājanam | rāja-kārya-paridhvaṃsī mantrī doṣeṇa lipyate
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- भोगस्य भाजनं राजा न राजा कार्य-भाजनम् | राज-कार्य-परिध्वंसी मन्त्री दोषेण लिप्यते
full_translation: And also, the vessel of enjoyment is not the king; the vessel of duty is the king. The one who is involved in duty, the minister, is smeared by fault.

original_iast: varaṃ prāṇa-parityāgaḥ śirasā vāpi kartanam | na tu svāmi-padāvāpti-pātakecchor upekṣaṇam
transliterated_devanagari: वरं प्राण-परित्यागः शिरसा वापि कर्तनम् | न तु स्वामि-पदावाप्ति-पातकेच्छोर् उपेक्षणम्
full_translation: Better is the abandonment of life, or even cutting off the head, but not the neglect of the attainment of the master's position by the sinful.

original_iast: atyucchrite mantriṇi pārthive ca viṣṭabhya pādāv upatiṣṭhate śrīḥ | sā strī-svabhāvād asahā bharasya tayor dvayor ekataraṃ jahāti
transliterated_devanagari: अत्युच्छ्रिते मन्त्रिणि पार्थिवे च विष्टभ्य पादाव् उपतिष्ठते श्रीः | सा स्त्री-स्वभावाद् असहा भरस्य तयोर् द्वयोर् एकतरं जहाति
full_translation: In the exalted position of the king's counselor, having established her feet, that woman of prosperity stands; by nature, she is unbearable of the burden of those two and abandons one of them.

original_iast: aparaṃ ca- ekaṃ bhūmi-patiḥ karoti sacivaṃ rājye pramāṇaṃ yadā taṃ mohāt śrayate madaḥ sa ca madālasyena nirvidyate | nirviṇṇasya padaṃ karoti hṛdaye tasya svatantra-spṛhā- svātantrya-spṛhayā tataḥ sa nṛpateḥ prāṇān abhidruhyati
transliterated_devanagari: अपरं च- एकं भूमि-पतिः करोति सचिवं राज्ये प्रमाणं यदा तं मोहात् श्रयते मदः स च मदालस्येन निर्विद्यते | निर्विण्णस्य पदं करोति हृदये तस्य स्वतन्त्र-स्पृहा- स्वातन्त्र्य-स्पृहया ततः स नृपतेः प्राणान् अभिद्रुह्यति
full_translation: When another lord of the land acts as a minister in the kingdom, and when that pride takes refuge from delusion, he is freed from the intoxication of laziness. In the heart of the disillusioned, he makes a place for his independent desire for freedom; thereafter, he attacks the life of the king.

original_iast: anyac ca- viṣa-dagdhasya bhaktasya dantasya calitasya ca | amātyasya ca duṣṭasya mūlād uddharaṇaṃ sukham
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- विष-दग्धस्य भक्तस्य दन्तस्य चलितस्य च | अमात्यस्य च दुष्टस्य मूलाद् उद्धरणं सुखम्
full_translation: And also, the extraction from the root of the poison of the burnt devotee, the moved tooth, the minister, and the wicked is pleasant.

original_iast: kiṃ ca- yaḥ kuryāt sacivāyattāṃ śriyaṃ tad-vyasane sati | so 'ndhavaj jagatī-pālaḥ sīdet sañcārakair vinā
transliterated_devanagari: किं च- यः कुर्यात् सचिवायत्तां श्रियं तद-व्यसने सति | सो ऽन्धवज् जगती-पालः सीदेत् सञ्चारकइर् विना

word_by_word_translation.translation: the one dependent on the minister
