full_translation: What would he do, who is dependent on the minister for prosperity, when calamity strikes? He would sit like a blind man in the world, without the means of movement.

original_iast: na so 'sti puruṣo loke yo na kāmayate śriyam | parasya yuvatiṃ ramyāṃ sādaraṃ nekṣate'tra kaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: न सो ऽस्ति पुरुषो लोके यो न कामयते श्रियम् | परस्य युवतिं रम्यां सादरं नेक्षतेऽत्र कः
full_translation: There is no man in the world who does not desire the wealth of another beautiful young woman and looks upon her with respect.

original_iast: kurvann api vyalīkāni yaḥ priyaḥ priya eva saḥ | aśeṣa-doṣa-duṣṭo 'pi kāyaḥ kasya na vallabhaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: कुर्वन्न् अपि व्यलीकानि यः प्रियः प्रिय एव सः | अशेष-दोष-दुष्टो ऽपि कायः कस्य न वल्लभः
full_translation: Even if he does wicked deeds, he who is dear is indeed beloved, regardless of all the faults of the wicked body.

original_iast: anyac ca- apriyāṇy api kurvāṇo yaḥ priyaḥ priya eva saḥ | dagdha-mandira-sāre'pi kasya vahnāv anādaraḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- अप्रियाण्य् अपि कुर्वाणो यः प्रियः प्रिय एव सः | दग्ध-मन्दिर-सारेऽपि कस्य वह्नाव् अनादरः
full_translation: Moreover, he who does unpleasant things, indeed, is beloved; even in the essence of a burnt temple, whose fire is there no disrespect?

original_iast: yasminn evādhikaṃ cakṣur ārohayati pārthivaḥ | sute'mātye'py udāsīne sa lakṣmyāśrīyate janaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: यस्मिन्न् एवाधिकं चक्षुर् आरोहयति पार्थिवः | सुतेऽमात्येऽप्य् उदासीने स लक्ष्म्याश्रीयते जनः
full_translation: In which, indeed, the earthly eye elevates more, even in the indifferent minister, he is adorned with the prosperity of a person.

original_iast: śṛṇu deva ! apriyasyāpi pathyasya pariṇāmaḥ sukhāvahaḥ | vaktā śrotā ca yatrāsti ramante tatra sampadaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: शृणु देव ! अप्रियस्यापि पथ्यस्य परिणामः सुखावहः | वक्ता श्रोता च यत्रास्ति रमन्ते तत्र सम्पदः
full_translation: Listen, O deity, even the result of the unpleasant is beneficial and brings happiness; where there is a speaker and a listener, there prosperity delights.

original_iast: mūla-bhṛtyān parityajya nāgantūn pratimānayet | nātaḥ parataro doṣo rājya-bheda-karo yataḥ
transliterated_devanagari: मूल-भृत्यान् परित्यज्य नागन्तून् प्रतिमानयेत् | नातः परतरो दोषो राज्य-भेद-करो यतः
full_translation: One should measure the intruders by abandoning the root servants; for there is no greater fault that causes division in the kingdom.

original_iast: durjano nārjavaṃ yāti sevyamāno 'pi nityaśaḥ | sveda-nābhyañjanopāyaiḥ śvapuccham iva nāmitam
transliterated_devanagari: दुर्जनो नार्जवं याति सेव्यमानो ऽपि नित्यशः | स्वेद-नाभ्यञ्जनोपायइः श्वपुच्छम् इव नामितम्
full_translation: A wicked person, even when being served, goes not straight; daily, he is not adorned by means of sweat, like a dog’s tail.

original_iast: aparaṃ ca- svedito marditaś caiva rañjubhiḥ pariveṣṭitaḥ | mukto dvādaśabhir varṣaiḥ śva-pucchaḥ prakṛtiṃ gataḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अपरं च- स्वेदितो मर्दितश् चइव रञ्जुभिः परिवेष्टितः | मुक्तो द्वादशभिर् वर्षइः श्व-पुच्छः प्रकृतिं गतः
full_translation: Another, having been sweated and massaged, like surrounded by colors, freed by twelve years, tomorrow the tail has gone to nature.

original_iast: anyac ca- vardhanaṃ vā sammānaṃ khalānāṃ prītaye kutaḥ | phalanty amṛta-seke'pi na pathyāni viṣa-drumāḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- वर्धनं वा सम्मानं खलानां प्रीतये कुतः | फलन्त्य् अमृत-सेकेऽपि न पथ्यानि विष-द्रुमाः
full_translation: Moreover, from where do the trees of poison bear fruit, even if watered with nectar, for the sake of pleasure or honor of the wicked?

original_iast: ato 'haṃ bravīmi- apṛṣṭas tasya na brūyād yaś ca necchet parābhavam | eṣa eva satāṃ dharmo viparīto 'satāṃ mataḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अतो ऽहं ब्रवीमि- अपृष्टस् तस्य न ब्रूयाद् यश् च नेच्छेत् पराभवम् | एष एव सतां धर्मो विपरीतो ऽसतां मतः
full_translation: Therefore, I speak: when not asked, one should not speak of him who does not wish for defeat. This indeed is the dharma of the virtuous, which is the opposite of the opinion of the unvirtuous.

original_iast: snigdho 'kuśalān nivārayati yas tat karma yan nirmalaṃ sā strī yātu-vidhāyinī sa matimān yaḥ sadbhir abhyarcyate | sā śrīr yā na madaṃ karoti sa sukhī yas tṛṣṇayā mucyate tan mitraṃ yat kṛtrimaṃ sa puruṣo yaḥ khidyate nendriyaiḥ
transliterated_devanagari: स्निग्धो ऽकुशलान् निवारयति यस् तत् कर्म यन् निर्मलं सा स्त्री यातु-विधायिनी स मतिमान् यः सद्भिर् अभ्यर्च्यते | सा श्रीर् या न मदं करोति स सुखी यस् तृष्णया मुच्यते तन् मित्रं यत् कृत्रिमं स पुरुषो यः खिद्यते नेन्द्रियइः
full_translation: The affectionate one restrains the unskilled; that action which is pure, may that woman, who is wise and is worshipped by the good, go forth. That prosperity, which does not cause intoxication, makes one happy; he who is freed from desire is that friend, which is artificial; that man who is troubled by the senses.

original_iast: nṛpaḥ kāmāsakto gaṇayati na kārye na ca hitaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ svacchandaḥ pravicarati matto gaja iva | tato māna-dhmātaḥ sa patati yadā śoka-gahane tadā bhṛtye doṣān kṣipati na nijaṃ vetty avinayam
transliterated_devanagari: नृपः कामासक्तो गणयति न कार्ये न च हितं यथेष्टं स्वच्छन्दः प्रविचरति मत्तो गज इव | ततो मान-ध्मातः स पतति यदा शोक-गहने तदा भृत्ये दोषान् क्षिपति न निजं वेत्त्य् अविनयम्
full_translation: The king, attached to desire, counts neither actions nor what is beneficial; he wanders freely, intoxicated like an elephant. Then, when his honor is blown away, he falls. In deep sorrow, he then throws the faults onto the servant, not knowing his own indiscipline.

original_iast: na parasyāparādhena pareṣāṃ daṇḍam ācaret | ātmanāvagataṃ kṛtvā badhnīyāt pūjayec ca vā
transliterated_devanagari: न परस्यापराधेन परेषां दण्डम् आचरेत् | आत्मनावगतं कृत्वा बध्नीयात् पूजयेच् च वा
full_translation: One should not impose punishment on others due to the offense of another; having understood oneself, one should either bind or worship.

original_iast: tathā coktam- guṇa-doṣāv aniścitya vidhinaṃ graha-nigrahe | sva-nāśāya yathā nyasto darpāt sarpa-mukhe karaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: तथा चोक्तम- गुण-दोषाव् अनिश्चित्य विधिनं ग्रह-निग्रहे | स्व-नाशाय यथा न्यस्तो दर्पात् सर्प-मुखे करः
full_translation: Thus it is said that due to the uncertainty of qualities and faults, in the restraint of planets, for one's own destruction, as a hand is placed in the mouth of a snake from pride.

original_iast: mantra-bījam idaṃ guptaṃ rakṣaṇīyaṃ yathā tathā | manāg api na bhidyeta tad bhinnaṃ na prarohati
transliterated_devanagari: मन्त्र-बीजम् इदं गुप्तं रक्षणीयं यथा तथा | मनाग् अपि न भिद्येत तद् भिन्नं न प्ररोहति
full_translation: This hidden seed of the mantra should be protected; as such, it should not be broken even slightly, for that which is broken does not grow forth.

original_iast: kiṃ ca- ādeyasya pradeyasya kartavyasya ca karmaṇaḥ | kṣipram akriyamāṇasya kālaḥ pibati tad-rasam
transliterated_devanagari: किं च- आदेयस्य प्रदेयस्य कर्तव्यस्य च कर्मणः | क्षिप्रम् अक्रियमाणस्य कालः पिबति तद-रसम्

word_by_word_translation.translation: of the thing to be taken
of the thing to be given

full_translation: Moreover, the essence of the duty related to the thing to be taken and the thing to be given, as well as the action, is quickly consumed by the time that is not being acted upon.

original_iast: mantro yodhaḥ ivādhīraḥ sarvāṅgaiḥ saṃvṛtair api | ciraṃ na sahate sthātuṃ parebhyo bheda-śaṅkayā
transliterated_devanagari: मन्त्रो योधः इवाधीरः सर्वाङ्गइः संवृतइर् अपि | चिरं न सहते स्थातुं परेभ्यो भेद-शङ्कया
full_translation: The mantra, like a fearless warrior, surrounded by all limbs, cannot bear to stand for a long time, due to the doubt of division from others.

original_iast: sakṛd duṣṭaṃ tu yo mitraṃ punaḥ sandhātum icchati | sa mṛtyur eva gṛhṇāti garbham aśvatarī yathā
transliterated_devanagari: सकृद् दुष्टं तु यो मित्रं पुनः सन्धातुम् इच्छति | स मृत्युर् एव गृह्णाति गर्भम् अश्वतरी यथा
full_translation: Once, indeed, he who wishes to reconcile with a wicked friend, death takes him like a horse takes the womb.

original_iast: aṅgāṅgi-bhāvam ajñātvā kathaṃ sāmarthya-nirṇayaḥ | paśya ṭiṭṭibha-mātreṇa samudro vyākulīkṛtaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अङ्गाङ्गि-भावम् अज्ञात्वा कथं सामर्थ्य-निर्णयः | पश्य टिट्टिभ-मात्रेण समुद्रो व्याकुलीकृतः

word_by_word_translation.translation: the bird, possibly a type of bird

full_translation: How can one make a decision about capability without knowing the essence within the body, when the ocean is disturbed merely by the measure of a bird?

original_iast: parābhavaṃ paricchettuṃ yogyāyogyaṃ ca vetti yaḥ | astīha yasya vijñānaṃ kṛcchreṇāpi na sīdati
transliterated_devanagari: पराभवं परिच्छेत्तुं योग्यायोग्यं च वेत्ति यः | अस्तीह यस्य विज्ञानं कृच्छ्रेणापि न सीदति
full_translation: He who knows the worthy and unworthy to cut off destruction, whose knowledge does not falter even with difficulty, is here.

original_iast: api ca- anucita-kāryārambhaḥ svajana-virodho balīyasā spardhā | pramadā-jana-viśvāso mṛtyor dvārāṇi catvāri
transliterated_devanagari: अपि च- अनुचित-कार्यारम्भः स्वजन-विरोधो बलीयसा स्पर्धा | प्रमदा-जन-विश्वासो मृत्योर् द्वाराणि चत्वारि
full_translation: Also, the beginning of inappropriate work, the opposition of one's own people, stronger competition, delight, trust of the people, and the four doors of death.

original_iast: sampattayaḥ parādhīnāḥ sadā cittam anirvṛttam | sva-jīivite'py aviśvāsas teṣāṃ ye rāja-sevakāḥ
transliterated_devanagari: सम्पत्तयः पराधीनाः सदा चित्तम् अनिर्वृत्तम् | स्व-जीइवितेऽप्य् अविश्वासस् तेषां ये राज-सेवकाः
full_translation: Wealthy individuals, who are always dependent, have unsettled minds; even in their own lives, there is distrust among those who are servants of the king.

original_iast: ko 'rthān prāpya na garvito viṣayiṇaḥ kasyāpado 'staṃ gatāḥ strībhiḥ kasya na khaṇḍitaṃ bhuvi manaḥ ko vāsti rājñāṃ priyā | kaḥ kālasya bhujāntaraṃ na ca gataḥ ko 'rthī gato gauravaṃ ko vā durjana-vāgurāsu patitaḥ kṣemeṇa yātaḥ pumān
transliterated_devanagari: को ऽर्थान् प्राप्य न गर्वितो विषयिणः कस्यापदो ऽस्तं गताः स्त्रीभिः कस्य न खण्डितं भुवि मनः को वास्ति राज्ञां प्रिया | कः कालस्य भुजान्तरं न च गतः को ऽर्थी गतो गउरवं को वा दुर्जन-वागुरासु पतितः क्षेमेण यातः पुमान्
full_translation: Who, having attained objects, is not proud of the worldly? Whose path has been traversed by women? Whose mind is not broken on this earth? Who exists as the beloved of kings? Who has not departed from the realm of time and the body? Who is the seeker that has gone with weight? Who, or what wicked person has fallen in words and yet gone safely?

original_iast: majjann api payorāśau labdhvā sarpāvalambanam | na muñcati na cādatte tathā mugdho 'smi samprati
transliterated_devanagari: मज्जन्न् अपि पयोराशउ लब्ध्वा सर्पावलम्बनम् | न मुञ्चति न चादत्ते तथा मुग्धो ऽस्मि सम्प्रति
full_translation: Even while drowning in the ocean of milk, having obtained the support of a serpent, I do not release it, nor do I take it; thus, I am bewildered now.

original_iast: yataḥ- ekatra rāja-viśvāso naśyaty anyatra bāndhavaḥ | kiṃ karomi kva gacchāmi patit o duḥkha-sāgare
transliterated_devanagari: यतः- एकत्र राज-विश्वासो नश्यत्य् अन्यत्र बान्धवः | किं करोमि क्व गच्छामि पतित् ओ दुःख-सागरे
full_translation: From where does the trust of the king get lost when relatives are elsewhere? What should I do, where should I go, having fallen into the ocean of sorrow?

original_iast: durjana-gamyā nāryaḥ prāyeṇāpātra-bhṛd bhavati rājā | kṛpaṇānusāri ca dhanaṃ devo giri-jaladhi-varṣī ca
transliterated_devanagari: दुर्जन-गम्या नार्यः प्रायेणापात्र-भृद् भवति राजा | कृपणानुसारि च धनं देवो गिरि-जलधि-वर्षी च
full_translation: Women are generally approached by the wicked; the king becomes worthy of wealth by following the miser, and the god is like a mountain, the rain-bringer of the ocean.

original_iast: kaścid āśraya-saundaryād dhatte śobhām asajjanaḥ | pramadālocana-nyastaṃ malīmasam ivāñjanam
transliterated_devanagari: कश्चिद् आश्रय-सउन्दर्याद् धत्ते शोभाम् असज्जनः | प्रमदालोचन-न्यस्तं मलीमसम् इवाञ्जनम्
full_translation: Some shelter holds splendor from beauty, as if the unworthy have placed it like soiled collyrium of the beautiful-eyed.

original_iast: ārādhyamāno nṛpatiḥ prayatnān na toṣam āyāti kim atra citram | ayaṃ tv apūrva-pratimā-viśeṣo yaḥ sevyamāno riputām upaiti
transliterated_devanagari: आराध्यमानो नृपतिः प्रयत्नान् न तोषम् आयाति किम् अत्र चित्रम् | अयं त्व् अपूर्व-प्रतिमा-विशेषो यः सेव्यमानो रिपुताम् उपइति
full_translation: The king, being worshipped, does not find satisfaction from efforts; what is wonderful here is indeed this unprecedented idol, which, when served, approaches the enemy.

original_iast: nimittam uddiśya hi yaḥ prakupyati dhruvaṃ sa tasyāpagame prasīdati | akāraṇa-dveṣi manas tu yasya vai kathaṃ janas taṃ paritoṣayiṣyati
transliterated_devanagari: निमित्तम् उद्दिश्य हि यः प्रकुप्यति ध्रुवं स तस्यापगमे प्रसीदति | अकारण-द्वेषि मनस् तु यस्य वइ कथं जनस् तं परितोषयिष्यति
full_translation: Indeed, he who becomes angry for a cause, certainly becomes pleased upon his departure; but how will people satisfy him whose mind is a hater without reason?

original_iast: vijñaiḥ snigdhair upakṛtam api dveṣyatām eti kaiścit sākṣād anyair apakṛtam api prītim evopayāti | citraṃ citraṃ kim atha caritaṃ naikabhāvāśrayāṇāṃ sevā-dharmaḥ parama-gahano yoginām apy agamyaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: विज्ञइः स्निग्धइर् उपकृतम् अपि द्वेष्यताम् एति कइश्चित् साक्षाद् अन्यइर् अपकृतम् अपि प्रीतिम् एवोपयाति | चित्रं चित्रं किम् अथ चरितं नइकभावाश्रयाणां सेवा-धर्मः परम-गहनो योगिनाम् अप्य् अगम्यः

word_by_word_translation.translation: of those who do not have a single feeling

full_translation: Even if done by the knowledgeable and affectionate, it goes to be hated; some directly harm others, yet they also approach with affection. What a wonder it is! Then, the conduct of those who do not have a single feeling, service is the supreme dharma, deep and inaccessible even to yogis.

original_iast: anyac ca- kṛta-śatam asatsu naṣṭaṃ subhāṣita-śataṃ ca naṣṭam abudheṣu | vacana-śatam avacana-kare buddhi-śatam acetane naṣṭam
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- कृत-शतम् असत्सु नष्टं सुभाषित-शतं च नष्टम् अबुधेषु | वचन-शतम् अवचन-करे बुद्धि-शतम् अचेतने नष्टम्
full_translation: And also, a hundred good deeds done are destroyed in the unworthy; a hundred well-spoken words are destroyed among the ignorant; a hundred unspoken words are in the hands of intellect; a hundred are destroyed in the unconscious.

original_iast: kiṃ ca- candana-taruṣu bhujaṅgā jaleṣu kamalāni tatra ca grāhāḥ | guṇa-ghātinaś ca bhoge khalā na ca sukhāny avighnāni
transliterated_devanagari: किं च- चन्दन-तरुषु भुजङ्गा जलेषु कमलानि तत्र च ग्राहाः | गुण-घातिनश् च भोगे खला न च सुखान्य् अविघ्नानि
full_translation: What is there in the trees of sandalwood, in the waters of lotuses, where there are also crocodiles, destroyers of qualities, and where wicked pleasures are not obstructed?

original_iast: mūlaṃ bhujaṅgaiḥ kusumāni bhṛṅgaiḥ śākhāḥ plavaṅgaiḥ śikharāṇi bhallaiḥ | nāsty eva tac-candana-pādapasya yan nāśritaṃ duṣṭataraiś ca hiṃsraiḥ
transliterated_devanagari: मूलं भुजङ्गइः कुसुमानि भृङ्गइः शाखाः प्लवङ्गइः शिखराणि भल्लइः | नास्त्य् एव तच-चन्दन-पादपस्य यन् नाश्रितं दुष्टतरइश् च हिंस्रइः
full_translation: Indeed, there is no root that is not dependent on the wicked and cruel, such as the flowers by bees, branches by birds, peaks by arrows, and the sandalwood tree.

original_iast: dūrād ucchrita-pāṇir ādra-nayanaḥ protsāritārdhāsano gāḍhāliṅgana-tat-paraḥ priya-kathā-praśneṣu dattādaraḥ | antarbhūta-viṣo bahir madhumayaś cātīva māyā-paṭuḥ ko nāmāyam apūrva-nāṭaka-vidhir yaḥ śikṣito durjanaiḥ
transliterated_devanagari: दूराद् उच्छ्रित-पाणिर् आद्र-नयनः प्रोत्सारितार्धासनो गाढालिङ्गन-तत-परः प्रिय-कथा-प्रश्नेषु दत्तादरः | अन्तर्भूत-विषो बहिर् मधुमयश् चातीव माया-पटुः को नामायम् अपूर्व-नाटक-विधिर् यः शिक्षितो दुर्जनइः
full_translation: From afar, a raised hand with moist eyes, encouraged in a half-seated position, deeply embraces that other beloved story, given respect in questions. Internally, there is poison, externally sweet; exceedingly skilled in illusion, who is this extraordinary method of drama that is educated by the wicked?

original_iast: poto dustara-vāri-rāśitaraṇe dīpo 'ndhakārāgame nirvāte vyajanaṃ madāndha-kariṇāṃ darpopaśāntyai sṛṇiḥ | itthaṃ tad bhuvi nāsti yasya vidhinā nopāya-cintā kṛtā manye durjana-citta-vṛtti-haraṇe dhātāpi bhagnodyamaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: पोतो दुस्तर-वारि-राशितरणे दीपो ऽन्धकारागमे निर्वाते व्यजनं मदान्ध-करिणां दर्पोपशान्त्यइ सृणिः | इत्थं तद् भुवि नास्ति यस्य विधिना नोपाय-चिन्ता कृता मन्ये दुर्जन-चित्त-वृत्ति-हरणे धातापि भग्नोद्यमः
full_translation: The boat is difficult to cross in the water of the ocean; a lamp is absent in the arrival of darkness. In the absence of a fan, the intoxication of elephants calms the pride. Thus, on earth, there is nothing of which, by destiny, there is no means; I think that thoughts made for the wicked mind's activities are even the broken endeavors of the elements in their removal.

original_iast: yayor eva samaṃ vittaṃ yayor eva samaṃ balam | tayor vivādo mantavyo nottamādhamayoḥ kvacit
transliterated_devanagari: ययोर् एव समं वित्तं ययोर् एव समं बलम् | तयोर् विवादो मन्तव्यो नोत्तमाधमयोः क्वचित्

word_by_word_translation.translation: between the best and the worst

full_translation: Indeed, the wealth and strength of those two are equal; a dispute between them should be considered, whether it be in the context of the best or the worst.

original_iast: ayuddhe hi yadā paśyen na kāñcid hitam ātmanaḥ | yudhyamānas tadā prājño mriyate ripuṇā saha
transliterated_devanagari: अयुद्धे हि यदा पश्येन् न काञ्चिद् हितम् आत्मनः | युध्यमानस् तदा प्राज्ञो म्रियते रिपुणा सह
full_translation: Indeed, when one sees no benefit for oneself while engaged in fighting, then the wise person dies together with the enemy.

original_iast: bhūmy-eka-deśasya guṇānvitasya bhṛtyasya vā buddhimataḥ praṇāśaḥ | bhṛtya-praṇāśo maraṇaṃ nṛpāṇāṃ naṣṭāpi bhūmiḥ sulabhā na bhṛtyāḥ
transliterated_devanagari: भूम्य-एक-देशस्य गुणान्वितस्य भृत्यस्य वा बुद्धिमतः प्रणाशः | भृत्य-प्रणाशो मरणं नृपाणां नष्टापि भूमिः सुलभा न भृत्याः
full_translation: The earth of a country endowed with qualities, or the destruction of a wise servant, is not the death of kings; even if lost, the earth is easily obtainable, not for the servant.

original_iast: pitā vā yadi vā bhrātā putrī vā yadi vā suhṛt | prāṇa-ccheda-karā rājñā hantavyā bhūtim icchatā
transliterated_devanagari: पिता वा यदि वा भ्राता पुत्री वा यदि वा सुहृत् | प्राण-च्छेद-करा राज्ञा हन्तव्या भूतिम् इच्छता
full_translation: Whether it is a father, or if it is a brother, or a daughter, or if it is a friend, life should be cut off by the king for the sake of desiring prosperity.

original_iast: api ca- dharmārtha-kāma-tattvajño naikānta-karuṇo bhavet | nahi hastastham apy annaṃ kṣamāvān bhakṣituṃ kṣamaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अपि च- धर्मार्थ-काम-तत्त्वज्ञो नइकान्त-करुणो भवेत् | नहि हस्तस्थम् अप्य् अन्नं क्षमावान् भक्षितुं क्षमः
full_translation: Moreover, one who knows the essence of righteousness, wealth, and desire, and is not indifferent and compassionate, is not able to consume even food that is in hand if he is forgiving.

original_iast: kiṃ ca- kṣamā śatrau ca mitre ca yatīnām eva bhūṣaṇam | aparādhiṣu sattveṣu nṛpāṇāṃ saiva dūṣaṇam
transliterated_devanagari: किं च- क्षमा शत्रउ च मित्रे च यतीनाम् एव भूषणम् | अपराधिषु सत्त्वेषु नृपाणां सइव दूषणम्
full_translation: Forgiveness is indeed an ornament for ascetics, both for friends and enemies; it is also a defilement among beings in the offenses of kings.

original_iast: aparaṃ ca- rājya-lobhād ahaṅkārād icchataḥ svāminaḥ padam | prāyaścittaṃ tu tasyaikaṃ jīvotsargo na cāparam
transliterated_devanagari: अपरं च- राज्य-लोभाद् अहङ्काराद् इच्छतः स्वामिनः पदम् | प्रायश्चित्तं तु तस्यइकं जीवोत्सर्गो न चापरम्
full_translation: Another atonement for the master, desiring a position from greed and pride, is the giving up of life; there is no other.

original_iast: rājā ghṛṇī brāhmaṇaḥ sarva-bhakṣī strī cāvajñā duṣprakṛtiḥ sahāyaḥ | preṣyaḥ pratīpo 'dhikṛtaḥ pramādī tyājyā ime yaś ca kṛtaṃ na vetti
transliterated_devanagari: राजा घृणी ब्राह्मणः सर्व-भक्षी स्त्री चावज्ञा दुष्प्रकृतिः सहायः | प्रेष्यः प्रतीपो ऽधिकृतः प्रमादी त्याज्या इमे यश् च कृतं न वेत्ति
full_translation: The king, the generous Brahmin, all eaters, and the woman who disrespects, the one with an evil nature, the helper who is sent, the one who is to be honored, the authorized, the careless—these should be abandoned, for they do not know what has been done.

original_iast: satyānṛtā ca paruṣā priya-vādinī ca hiṃsrā dayālur api cārtha-parā vadānyā | nitya-vyayā pracura-ratna-dhanāgamā ca vārāṅganeva nṛpa-nītir aneka-rūpā
transliterated_devanagari: सत्यानृता च परुषा प्रिय-वादिनी च हिंस्रा दयालुर् अपि चार्थ-परा वदान्या | नित्य-व्यया प्रचुर-रत्न-धनागमा च वाराङ्गनेव नृप-नीतिर् अनेक-रूपा
full_translation: Truth and falsehood, harshness and beloved speech, violence and compassion, also for the purpose of superior praise, eternal expenditure, abundant gems and wealth, like a beautiful maiden, the king's policy takes many forms.

original_iast: suhṛd-bhedas tāvad bhavatu bhavatāṃ śatru-nilaye khalaḥ kālākṛṣṭaḥ pralayam upasarpatv ahar-ahaḥ | jano nityaṃ bhūyāt sakala-sukha-sampatti-vasatiḥ kathārambhe rambhye satatam iha bālo 'pi ramatām
transliterated_devanagari: सुहृद-भेदस् तावद् भवतु भवतां शत्रु-निलये खलः कालाकृष्टः प्रलयम् उपसर्पत्व् अहर-अहः | जनो नित्यं भूयात् सकल-सुख-सम्पत्ति-वसतिः कथारम्भे रम्भ्ये सततम् इह बालो ऽपि रमताम्
full_translation: May there be no division among friends as long as there are enemies dwelling in the abode of wickedness, drawn by time towards destruction. May the people, day and night, always experience all happiness and prosperity in their residence. In the beginning of stories, may there always be enjoyment here, so that even a child may play.

original_iast: haṃsaiḥ saha mayūrāṇāṃ vigrahe tulya-vikrame | viśvāsya vañcitā haṃsāḥ kākaiḥ sthitvāri-mandire
transliterated_devanagari: हंसइः सह मयूराणां विग्रहे तुल्य-विक्रमे | विश्वास्य वञ्चिता हंसाः काकइः स्थित्वारि-मन्दिरे
full_translation: The swans, deceived by the crows, stood together with the peacocks in the form of equal valor in the temple, having confidence in their enemy.

original_iast: yadi na syān narapatiḥ samyaṅ-netā tataḥ prajā | akarṇa-dhārā jaladhau viplaveteha naur iva
transliterated_devanagari: यदि न स्यान् नरपतिः सम्यङ-नेता ततः प्रजा | अकर्ण-धारा जलधउ विप्लवेतेह नउर् इव
full_translation: If the king is not a proper leader, then the subjects will be like a boat that is deaf to the flow of water and will be drowned.

original_iast: aparaṃ ca- prajāṃ saṃrakṣati nṛpaḥ sā vardhayati pārthivam | vardhanād rakṣaṇaṃ śreyas tad-abhāve sad apy asat
transliterated_devanagari: अपरं च- प्रजां संरक्षति नृपः सा वर्धयति पार्थिवम् | वर्धनाद् रक्षणं श्रेयस् तद-अभावे सद् अप्य् असत्
full_translation: Furthermore, the king protects the populace; that nurtures the earthly welfare. In the absence of such nurturing, even good is not present, but bad prevails.

original_iast: payaḥ-pānaṃ bhujaṅgānāṃ kevalaṃ viṣa-vardhanam | upadeśo hi mūrkhāṇāṃ prakopāya na śāntaye
transliterated_devanagari: पयः-पानं भुजङ्गानां केवलं विष-वर्धनम् | उपदेशो हि मूर्खाणां प्रकोपाय न शान्तये
full_translation: Drinking milk is indeed only an increase of poison for serpents; instruction for fools is not for peace but for agitation.

original_iast: anyac ca- vidvān evopadeṣṭavyo nāvidvāṃs tu kadācana | vānarānupadiśyātha sthāna-bhraṣṭā yayuḥ khagāḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- विद्वान् एवोपदेष्टव्यो नाविद्वांस् तु कदाचन | वानरानुपदिश्याथ स्थान-भ्रष्टा ययुः खगाः
full_translation: And also, indeed, the learned should be instructed, not the ignorant; at any time, instructing the monkeys, thereafter, the place was corrupted, and they (the birds) went.

original_iast: asmābhir nirmitā nīḍāś cañcu-mātrāhṛtais tṛṇaiḥ | hasta-pādādi-saṃyuktā yūyaṃ kim avasīdatha
transliterated_devanagari: अस्माभिर् निर्मिता नीडाश् चञ्चु-मात्राहृतइस् तृणइः | हस्त-पादादि-संयुक्ता यूयं किम् अवसीदथ
full_translation: What are you lamenting, you who are joined together with nests created by us, taken only from the beak, and made from grass, hand, foot, etc.?

original_iast: anyadā bhūṣaṇaṃ puṃsaḥ kṣamā lajjeva yoṣitaḥ | parākramaḥ paribhave vaiyātyaṃ surateṣv iva
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यदा भूषणं पुंसः क्षमा लज्जेव योषितः | पराक्रमः परिभवे वइयात्यं सुरतेष्व् इव
full_translation: At another time, the ornament of a man is indeed forgiveness; the shame of a woman is valor, like the nobility found in pleasures.

original_iast: rājā vihasyāha- ātmanaś ca pareṣāṃ ca yaḥ samīkṣya balābalam | antaraṃ naiva jānāti sa tiraskriyate'ribhiḥ
transliterated_devanagari: राजा विहस्याह- आत्मनश् च परेषां च यः समीक्ष्य बलाबलम् | अन्तरं नइव जानाति स तिरस्क्रियतेऽरिभिः
full_translation: A king who, laughing, does not know the difference between his own strength and the strength of others, is disregarded by his enemies.

original_iast: suciraṃ hi caran nityaṃ kṣetre satyam abuddhimān | dvīpi-carma-paricchanno vāg-doṣād gardabho hataḥ
transliterated_devanagari: सुचिरं हि चरन् नित्यं क्षेत्रे सत्यम् अबुद्धिमान् | द्वीपि-चर्म-परिच्छन्नो वाग-दोषाद् गर्दभो हतः

word_by_word_translation.translation: the one who is not wise

full_translation: Indeed, for a long time, wandering always in the field of truth, the one who is not wise, covered by the skin of the island, due to the fault of speech, is killed like an ass.

original_iast: sevitavyo mahā-vṛkṣaḥ phala-cchāyā-samanvitaḥ | yadi daivāt phalaṃ nāsti cchāyā kena nivāryate
transliterated_devanagari: सेवितव्यो महा-वृक्षः फल-च्छाया-समन्वितः | यदि दइवात् फलं नास्ति च्छाया केन निवार्यते
full_translation: A great tree, accompanied by fruit and shade, if by chance there is no fruit, by whom is the shade prevented?

original_iast: anyac ca- hīna-sevā na kartavyā kartavyo mahad āśrayaḥ | payo 'pi śauṇḍikī-haste vāruṇĪty abhidhīyate
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- हीन-सेवा न कर्तव्या कर्तव्यो महद् आश्रयः | पयो ऽपि शउण्डिकी-हस्ते वारुणĪत्य् अभिधीयते
full_translation: Furthermore, inferior service should not be performed; a great shelter, even milk, is referred to as being in the vessel in the hand of Varuna.

original_iast: anyac ca- mahān apy alpatāṃ yāti nirguṇe guṇa-vistaraḥ | ādhārādheya-bhāvena gajendra iva darpaṇe
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- महान् अप्य् अल्पतां याति निर्गुणे गुण-विस्तरः | आधाराधेय-भावेन गजेन्द्र इव दर्पणे
full_translation: And also, even the great goes to smallness in the quality-less; like the king of elephants in a mirror, the expansion of quality is both a basis and dependent.

original_iast: kintu- ajā siṃha-prasādena vane carati nirbhayam | rāmam āsādya laṅkāyāṃ lebhe rājyaṃ vibhīṣaṇaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: किन्तु- अजा सिंह-प्रसादेन वने चरति निर्भयम् | रामम् आसाद्य लङ्कायां लेभे राज्यं विभीषणः
full_translation: But Vibhishana, having approached Rama fearlessly in the forest, obtained the kingdom in Lanka by the grace of the lion (Rama).

original_iast: viśeṣataś ca- vyapadeśe'pi siddhiḥ syād atiśakte narādhipe | śaśino vyapadeśena śaśakāḥ sukham āsate
transliterated_devanagari: विशेषतश् च- व्यपदेशेऽपि सिद्धिः स्याद् अतिशक्ते नराधिपे | शशिनो व्यपदेशेन शशकाः सुखम् आसते

word_by_word_translation.translation: even in the context of designation

full_translation: Especially in the context of designation, success may be found in the powerful king of men; by the designation of the moon, rabbits dwell in happiness.

original_iast: spṛśann api gajo hanti jighrann api bhujaṅgamaḥ | pālayann api bhūpālaḥ prahasann api durjanaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: स्पृशन्न् अपि गजो हन्ति जिघ्रन्न् अपि भुजङ्गमः | पालयन्न् अपि भूपालः प्रहसन्न् अपि दुर्जनः
full_translation: Even while touching, the elephant kills; even while smelling, the serpent protects; even while laughing, the king is a wicked person.

original_iast: vijayo brūte- udyateṣv api śastreṣu dūto vadati nānyathā | sadaivāvadhya-bhāvena yathārthasya hi vācakaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: विजयो ब्रूते- उद्यतेष्व् अपि शस्त्रेषु दूतो वदति नान्यथा | सदइवावध्य-भावेन यथार्थस्य हि वाचकः
full_translation: The messenger speaks of victory, also in the context of rising weapons; otherwise, the truth is unwavering, like the essence of the speaker of the truth.

original_iast: svadeśajaṃ kulācāra-viśuddham upadhāśucim | mantrajñam avasaninaṃ vyabhicāra-vivarjitam
transliterated_devanagari: स्वदेशजं कुलाचार-विशुद्धम् उपधाशुचिम् | मन्त्रज्ञम् अवसनिनं व्यभिचार-विवर्जितम्
full_translation: One who is of one's own country, adheres to family traditions, is pure in conduct, knowledgeable in mantras, humble, and abstains from deviation.

original_iast: adhīta-vyavahārārthaṃ maulaṃ khyātaṃ vipaścitam | arthasyotpādakaṃ caiva vidadhyān mantriṇaṃ nṛpaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अधीत-व्यवहारार्थं मउलं ख्यातं विपश्चितम् | अर्थस्योत्पादकं चइव विदध्यान् मन्त्रिणं नृपः
full_translation: The king, who is wise and known for the root of practical purposes, should maintain the minister who produces meaning.

original_iast: rājā mattaḥ śiśuś caiva pramadā dhana-garvitaḥ | aprāpyam api vāñchanti kiṃ punar labhyate'pi yat
transliterated_devanagari: राजा मत्तः शिशुश् चइव प्रमदा धन-गर्वितः | अप्राप्यम् अपि वाञ्छन्ति किं पुनर् लभ्यतेऽपि यत्
full_translation: Even an intoxicated king, a child, and a beautiful woman, though they desire what is unattainable, what can be obtained again?

original_iast: bhakto guṇī śucir dakṣaḥ pragalbho 'vyasanī kṣamī | brāhmaṇaḥ paramarmajño dūtaḥ syāt pratibhānavān
transliterated_devanagari: भक्तो गुणी शुचिर् दक्षः प्रगल्भो ऽव्यसनी क्षमी | ब्राह्मणः परमर्मज्ञो दूतः स्यात् प्रतिभानवान्
full_translation: A devoted, virtuous, pure, skilled, mature, unwavering, forgiving Brahmin, who knows the ultimate truth, may be an insightful messenger.

original_iast: prasādaṃ kurute patyuḥ sampattiṃ nābhivāñchati | kālimā kālakūṭasya nāpaitīśvara-saṅgamāt
transliterated_devanagari: प्रसादं कुरुते पत्युः सम्पत्तिं नाभिवाञ्छति | कालिमा कालकूटस्य नापइतीश्वर-सङ्गमात्
full_translation: She who bestows grace upon her husband does not desire wealth; she does not even fear the darkness of the poison that comes from the union with God.

original_iast: khalaḥ karoti durvṛttaṃ nūnaṃ phalati sādhuṣu | daśānano 'harat sītāṃ bandhanaṃ syān mahodadheḥ
transliterated_devanagari: खलः करोति दुर्वृत्तं नूनं फलति साधुषु | दशाननो ऽहरत् सीतां बन्धनं स्यान् महोदधेः

word_by_word_translation.translation: the ten-faced one, referring to Ravana

full_translation: The wicked certainly performs evil deeds; among the good, the ten-faced one took Sita into bondage from the great ocean.

original_iast: aparaṃ ca- na sthātavyaṃ na gantavyaṃ durjanena samaṃ kvacit | kāka-saṅgād dhato haṃsas tiṣṭhan gachaṃś ca vartakaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अपरं च- न स्थातव्यं न गन्तव्यं दुर्जनेन समं क्वचित् | काक-सङ्गाद् धतो हंसस् तिष्ठन् गछंश् च वर्तकः
full_translation: One should neither stay nor go anywhere equally with the wicked; like a swan standing apart from the company of crows, the potter should go.

original_iast: durjanair ucyamānāni saṃmatāni priyāṇy api | akāla-kusumānīva bhayaṃ saṃjanayanti hi
transliterated_devanagari: दुर्जनइर् उच्यमानानि संमतानि प्रियाण्य् अपि | अकाल-कुसुमानीव भयं संजनयन्ति हि
full_translation: Indeed, even the beloved flowers, when spoken of by wicked people, generate fear like untimely blossoms.

original_iast: pratyakṣe'pi kṛte doṣe mūrkhaḥ sāntvena tuṣyati | ratha-kāro nijāṃ bhāryāṃ sajārāṃ śirasākarot
transliterated_devanagari: प्रत्यक्षेऽपि कृते दोषे मूर्खः सान्त्वेन तुष्यति | रथ-कारो निजां भार्यां सजारां शिरसाकरोत्
full_translation: Even when a fault is evident, a fool is pleased by consolation; the chariot maker places his wife, who has a child, on his head.

original_iast: paruṣāṇy api yā proktā dṛṣṭā yā krodha-cakṣuṣā | suprasanna-mukhī bhartuḥ sā nārī dharma-bhājanam
transliterated_devanagari: परुषाण्य् अपि या प्रोक्ता दृष्टा या क्रोध-चक्षुषा | सुप्रसन्न-मुखी भर्तुः सा नारी धर्म-भाजनम्
full_translation: A woman who is harsh yet also spoken of, who is seen with the eyes of anger, yet has a well-pleased face towards her husband, is indeed a vessel of dharma.

original_iast: aparaṃ ca- nagarastho vanastho vā pāpo vā yadi vā śuciḥ | yāsāṃ strīṇāṃ priyo bhartā tāsāṃ lokā mahodayāḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अपरं च- नगरस्थो वनस्थो वा पापो वा यदि वा शुचिः | यासां स्त्रीणां प्रियो भर्ता तासां लोका महोदयाः

word_by_word_translation.translation: one who is in the city
one who is in the forest

full_translation: Whether one is another who resides in the city, or one who lives in the forest, or is sinful, or is pure, the husband who is beloved by such women is greatly esteemed in the worlds.

original_iast: anyac ca- bhartā hi paramaṃ nāryā bhūṣaṇaṃ bhūṣaṇair vinā | eṣā virahitā tena śobhanāpi na śobhate
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- भर्ता हि परमं नार्या भूषणं भूषणइर् विना | एषा विरहिता तेन शोभनापि न शोभते
full_translation: And also, indeed, the husband is the supreme ornament of a woman; without ornaments, this one, being separated, does not shine even beautifully.

original_iast: tisraḥ koṭyo 'rdha-koṭī ca yāni lomāni mānave | tāvat kālaṃ vaset svarge bhartāraṃ yo 'nugacchati
transliterated_devanagari: तिस्रः कोट्यो ऽर्ध-कोटी च यानि लोमानि मानवे | तावत् कालं वसेत् स्वर्गे भर्तारं यो ऽनुगच्छति
full_translation: As long as the hairs of a man amount to three and a half crores, he may dwell in heaven who follows his husband.

original_iast: anyac ca- vyāla-grāhī yathā vyālaṃ balād uddharate bilāt | tadvad bhartāram ādāya svarga-loke mahīyate
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- व्याल-ग्राही यथा व्यालं बलाद् उद्धरते बिलात् | तद्वद् भर्तारम् आदाय स्वर्ग-लोके महीयते
full_translation: And also, just as the serpent that seizes by force raises itself from the hole, similarly, the husband, taking [his wife], is honored in the heavenly world.

original_iast: citau pariṣvajya vicetanaṃ patiṃ priyā hi yā muñcati deham ātmanaḥ | kṛtvāpi pāpaṃ śata-lakṣam apy asau patiṃ gṛhītvā sura-lokam āpnuyāt
transliterated_devanagari: चितउ परिष्वज्य विचेतनं पतिं प्रिया हि या मुञ्चति देहम् आत्मनः | कृत्वापि पापं शत-लक्षम् अप्य् असउ पतिं गृहीत्वा सुर-लोकम् आप्नुयात्
full_translation: Indeed, the beloved who embraces her conscious husband in the heart, even after committing a hundred thousand sins, may attain the divine realm by taking that husband.

original_iast: yataḥ- yasmai dadyāt pitā tv enāṃ bhrātā vānumate pituḥ | taṃ śuśrūṣeta jīvantaṃ saṃsthitaṃ ca na laṅghayet
transliterated_devanagari: यतः- यस्मइ दद्यात् पिता त्व् एनां भ्राता वानुमते पितुः | तं शुश्रूषेत जीवन्तं संस्थितं च न लङ्घयेत्
full_translation: From whom a father may give to her, the brother should serve that living and established one with the father's permission and should not transgress.

original_iast: śataṃ dadyān na vivaded iti vijñasya saṃmatam | vinā hetum api dvandvam etan mūrkhasya lakṣaṇam
transliterated_devanagari: शतं दद्यान् न विवदेद् इति विज्ञस्य संमतम् | विना हेतुम् अपि द्वन्द्वम् एतन् मूर्खस्य लक्षणम्
full_translation: A hundred should be given; thus, it is said that one should not argue without reason. This is a characteristic of the foolish.

original_iast: varṇākāra-pratidhvānair netra-vaktra-vikārataḥ | apy ūhanti mano dhīrās tasmād rahasi mantrayet
transliterated_devanagari: वर्णाकार-प्रतिध्वानइर् नेत्र-वक्त्र-विकारतः | अप्य् ऊहन्ति मनो धीरास् तस्माद् रहसि मन्त्रयेत्
full_translation: Even the wise, despite the distortions of the color-form reflected in the eyes and face, conjecture in secret. Therefore, one should deliberate.

original_iast: vedyānām āturaḥ śreyān vyasanī yo niyoginām | viduṣāṃ jīvanaṃ mūrkhaḥ sad-varṇo jīvanaṃ satām
transliterated_devanagari: वेद्यानाम् आतुरः श्रेयान् व्यसनी यो नियोगिनाम् | विदुषां जीवनं मूर्खः सद-वर्णो जीवनं सताम्
full_translation: A fool, who is afflicted and addicted, has a better life than the wise engaged in the lives of the virtuous.

original_iast: bhavet sva-para-rāṣṭrāṇāṃ kāryākāryāvalokane | cāraś cakṣur mahībhartur yasya nāsty andha eva saḥ
transliterated_devanagari: भवेत् स्व-पर-राष्ट्राणां कार्याकार्यावलोकने | चारश् चक्षुर् महीभर्तुर् यस्य नास्त्य् अन्ध एव सः

word_by_word_translation.translation: in the observation of duties and non-duties

full_translation: He who has four eyes, observing the duties and non-duties of his own and other nations, is indeed not blind, the lord of the earth.

original_iast: tīrthāśrama-sura-sthāne śāstara-vijñāna-hetunā | tapasvi-vyañjanopetaiḥ sva-caraiḥ saha saṃvaset
transliterated_devanagari: तीर्थाश्रम-सुर-स्थाने शास्तर-विज्ञान-हेतुना | तपस्वि-व्यञ्जनोपेतइः स्व-चरइः सह संवसेत्
full_translation: In a divine place, the pilgrimage hermitage, for the purpose of knowledge of scriptures, may the ascetic endowed with qualities conduct himself together with his own nature.

original_iast: ṣaṭ-karṇo bhidyate mantras tathā prāptaś ca vārtayā | ity ātmanā dvitīyena mantraḥ kāryo mahī-bhṛtā
transliterated_devanagari: षट-कर्णो भिद्यते मन्त्रस् तथा प्राप्तश् च वार्तया | इत्य् आत्मना द्वितीयेन मन्त्रः कार्यो मही-भृता
full_translation: The six ears are pierced by the mantra, and thus obtained by the word; the second mantra is to be performed by the self, carried by the earth.

original_iast: paśya- mantra-bhede hi ye doṣā bhavanti pṛthivī-pateḥ | na śakyās te samādhātum iti nīti-vidāṃ matam
transliterated_devanagari: पश्य- मन्त्र-भेदे हि ये दोषा भवन्ति पृथिवी-पतेः | न शक्यास् ते समाधातुम् इति नीति-विदां मतम्
full_translation: "Look, indeed, in the division of the mantra, those faults that arise from the lord of the earth cannot be resolved; thus is the opinion of the wise regarding policy."

original_iast: sa kiṃ bhṛtyaḥ sa kiṃ mantrī ya ādāv eva bhūpatim | yuddhodyogaṃ sva-bhū-tyāgaṃ nirdiśaty avicāritam
transliterated_devanagari: स किं भृत्यः स किं मन्त्री य आदाव् एव भूपतिम् | युद्धोद्योगं स्व-भू-त्यागं निर्दिशत्य् अविचारितम्
full_translation: What is a servant? What is a minister? Indeed, who in the beginning indicates the king's effort of war and the abandonment of his own land, unthought-of?

original_iast: anyac ca- sāmnā dānena bhedena samastair athavā pṛthak | sādhituṃ prayatetārīn na yuddhena kadācana
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- साम्ना दानेन भेदेन समस्तइर् अथवा पृथक् | साधितुं प्रयतेतारीन् न युद्धेन कदाचन
full_translation: And also, by means of agreement, by donation, or by division, one should strive to achieve everything separately; not by war at any time.

original_iast: aparaṃ ca- sarva eva janaḥ śūro hy anāsādita-vigrahaḥ | adṛṣṭa-para-sāmarthyaḥ sa-darpaḥ ko bhaven na hi
transliterated_devanagari: अपरं च- सर्व एव जनः शूरो ह्य् अनासादित-विग्रहः | अदृष्ट-पर-सामर्थ्यः स-दर्पः को भवेन् न हि
full_translation: Indeed, all people are brave; he is unconquered in battle, possessing unseen superior capabilities. Who would not become proud?

original_iast: kiṃ ca- na tathotthāpyate grāvā prāṇibhir dāruṇā yathā | alpopāyān mahā-siddhir etan-mantra-phalaṃ mahat
transliterated_devanagari: किं च- न तथोत्थाप्यते ग्रावा प्राणिभिर् दारुणा यथा | अल्पोपायान् महा-सिद्धिर् एतन-मन्त्र-फलं महत्
full_translation: What is more, the earth is not raised in that way by living beings harshly, as great success is achieved through this mantra with little means.

original_iast: yathā kāla-kṛtodyogāt kṛṣiḥ phalavatī bhavet | tadvan nītir iyaṃ deva cirāt phalati na kṣaṇāt
transliterated_devanagari: यथा काल-कृतोद्योगात् कृषिः फलवती भवेत् | तद्वन् नीतिर् इयं देव चिरात् फलति न क्षणात्
full_translation: Just as agriculture becomes fruitful from the effort made over time, similarly, this policy, O God, bears fruit not in a moment but over a long period.

original_iast: aparaṃ ca- dūre bhīrutvam āsanne śūratā mahato guṇaḥ | vipattau hi mahān loke dhīratvam adhigacchati
transliterated_devanagari: अपरं च- दूरे भीरुत्वम् आसन्ने शूरता महतो गुणः | विपत्तउ हि महान् लोके धीरत्वम् अधिगच्छति
full_translation: Another quality of greatness is that courage attains in the world, indeed, in adversity, while fearfulness is found near.

original_iast: anyac ca- pratyūhaḥ sarva-siddhīnām uttāpaḥ prathamaḥ kila | atiśītalam apy ambhaḥ kiṃ bhinatti na bhūbhṛtaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- प्रत्यूहः सर्व-सिद्धीनाम् उत्तापः प्रथमः किल | अतिशीतलम् अप्य् अम्भः किं भिनत्ति न भूभृतः
full_translation: And also, the counteraction of all accomplishments is indeed the first rise; even very cold water does not break the earth-holder.

original_iast: balinā saha yoddhavyam iti nāsti nidarśanam | tad yuddhaṃ hastinā sārdhaṃ narāṇāṃ mṛtyum āvahet
transliterated_devanagari: बलिना सह योद्धव्यम् इति नास्ति निदर्शनम् | तद् युद्धं हस्तिना सार्धं नराणां मृत्युम् आवहेत्
full_translation: There is no example that a battle should be fought with strength together; that battle would bring death to men along with the elephant.

original_iast: anyac ca- sa mūrkhaḥ kālam aprāpya yo 'pakartari vartate | kalir balavatā sārdhaṃ kīṭa-pakṣodgamo yathā
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- स मूर्खः कालम् अप्राप्य यो ऽपकर्तरि वर्तते | कलिर् बलवता सार्धं कीट-पक्षोद्गमो यथा
full_translation: And also, that fool who does not attain time exists in the doer, just as in the age of Kali, with strength, the rise of wings of an insect.

original_iast: kiṃ ca- kaurmaṃ saṅkocam āsthāya prahāram api marṣayet | prāpta-kāle tu nītijña uttiṣṭhet krūra-sarpavat
transliterated_devanagari: किं च- कउर्मं सङ्कोचम् आस्थाय प्रहारम् अपि मर्षयेत् | प्राप्त-काले तु नीतिज्ञ उत्तिष्ठेत् क्रूर-सर्पवत्
full_translation: What, then, should the tortoise do? Having taken withdrawal, it should also suppress the attack. However, at the right time, the one knowledgeable in ethics should arise like a cruel serpent.

original_iast: mahaty alpe'py upāyajñaḥ samam eva bhavet kṣamaḥ | samunmūlayituṃ vṛkṣāṃs tṛṇānīva nadīrayaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: महत्य् अल्पेऽप्य् उपायज्ञः समम् एव भवेत् क्षमः | समुन्मूलयितुं वृक्षांस् तृणानीव नदीरयः
full_translation: Even a person who knows the means, even in small matters, may indeed become capable of completely uprooting trees like grass from the rivers.

original_iast: ekaḥ śataṃ yodhayati prākāra-stho dhanurdharaḥ | śataṃ śata-sahasrāṇi tasmād durgaṃ viśiṣyate
transliterated_devanagari: एकः शतं योधयति प्राकार-स्थो धनुर्धरः | शतं शत-सहस्राणि तस्माद् दुर्गं विशिष्यते
full_translation: One archer fights against a hundred; therefore, the fort is distinguished by the thousands of archers standing on the walls.

original_iast: kiṃ ca- adurga-viṣayaḥ kasya nāreḥ paribhavāspadam | adurgo 'nāśrayo rājā pota-cyuta-manuṣyavat
transliterated_devanagari: किं च- अदुर्ग-विषयः कस्य नारेः परिभवास्पदम् | अदुर्गो ऽनाश्रयो राजा पोत-च्युत-मनुष्यवत्
full_translation: What subject is not difficult for a woman in a place of distress? A king, like a castaway boat, is without support.

original_iast: durgaṃ kuryān mahākhātam ucca-prākāra-saṃyutam | sa-yantraṃ sa-jalaṃ śaila-sarin-maru-vanāśrayam
transliterated_devanagari: दुर्गं कुर्यान् महाखातम् उच्च-प्राकार-संयुतम् | स-यन्त्रं स-जलं शइल-सरिन-मरु-वनाश्रयम्
full_translation: One should create a fortress with a great pit, high walls joined together, that machine, and water, near the mountain, river, and desert forest refuge.

original_iast: vistīrṇatāti-vaiṣamyaṃ rasa-dhānyedhma-saṅgrahaḥ | praveśaś cāpa-sāraś ca saptaitā durga-sampadaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: विस्तीर्णताति-वइषम्यं रस-धान्येध्म-सङ्ग्रहः | प्रवेशश् चाप-सारश् च सप्तइता दुर्ग-सम्पदः
full_translation: The vastness and diversity of the essence of grains, the collection, the entrance, the bow, the essence, and here, the seven fortresses of wealth.

original_iast: yo yatra kuśalaḥ kārye taṃ tatra viniyojayet | karmasv adṛṣṭa-karmā yaḥ śāstrajño 'pi vimuhyati
transliterated_devanagari: यो यत्र कुशलः कार्ये तं तत्र विनियोजयेत् | कर्मस्व् अदृष्ट-कर्मा यः शास्त्रज्ञो ऽपि विमुह्यति
full_translation: Whoever is skilled in work should employ him there in his own work; even a knowledgeable person in scriptures becomes bewildered by unseen actions.

original_iast: dhānyānāṃ saṅgraho rājann uttamaḥ sarva-saṅgrahāt | nikṣiptaṃ hi mukhe ratnaṃ na kuryāt prāṇa-dhāraṇam
transliterated_devanagari: धान्यानां सङ्ग्रहो राजन्न् उत्तमः सर्व-सङ्ग्रहात् | निक्षिप्तं हि मुखे रत्नं न कुर्यात् प्राण-धारणम्
full_translation: O king, the collection of grains is indeed the best among all collections; one should not place a gem in the mouth for the sake of sustaining life.

original_iast: kiṃ ca- khyātaḥ sarva-rasānāṃ hi lavaṇo rasa uttamaḥ | gṛhṇīyāt taṃ vinā tena vyañjanaṃ gomayāyate
transliterated_devanagari: किं च- ख्यातः सर्व-रसानां हि लवणो रस उत्तमः | गृह्णीयात् तं विना तेन व्यञ्जनं गोमयायते
full_translation: Indeed, among all the tastes, salt is known to be the best; without it, the condiment is made from cow dung.

original_iast: ātma-pakṣaṃ parityajya para-pakṣeṣu yo rataḥ | sa parair hanyate mūḍho nīla-varṇa-śṛgālavat
transliterated_devanagari: आत्म-पक्षं परित्यज्य पर-पक्षेषु यो रतः | स परइर् हन्यते मूढो नील-वर्ण-शृगालवत्
full_translation: He who is attached to the side of others, having abandoned his own side, is harmed by others; he is a fool, like a blue-colored jackal.

original_iast: yaḥ svabhāvo hi yasyāsti sa nityaṃ duratikramaḥ | śvā yadi kriyate rājā tat kiṃ nāśnāty upānaham
transliterated_devanagari: यः स्वभावो हि यस्यास्ति स नित्यं दुरतिक्रमः | श्वा यदि क्रियते राजा तत् किं नाश्नात्य् उपानहम्
full_translation: Indeed, he whose nature is eternally difficult to transgress, if a king is treated like a dog, what food does he not eat?

original_iast: chidraṃ marma ca vīryaṃ ca sarvaṃ vetti nijo ripuḥ | dahaty antargataś caiva śuṣkaṃ vṛkṣam ivānalaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: छिद्रं मर्म च वीर्यं च सर्वं वेत्ति निजो रिपुः | दहत्य् अन्तर्गतश् चइव शुष्कं वृक्षम् इवानलः
full_translation: The enemy knows all, including the essence and potency; he burns the internal (part) like fire (burns) a dry tree.

original_iast: nandaṃ jaghāna cāṇakyas tīkṣṇa-dūta-prayogataḥ | tad dūrāntaritaṃ dūtaṃ paśyed vīra-samanvitaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: नन्दं जघान चाणक्यस् तीक्ष्ण-दूत-प्रयोगतः | तद् दूरान्तरितं दूतं पश्येद् वीर-समन्वितः
full_translation: Chanakya struck Nanda with a sharp messenger; the hero should see that messenger who has been sent from afar.

original_iast: na sā sabhā yatra na santi vṛddhā vṛddhā na te ye na vadanti dharmam | dharmaḥ sa no yatra na satyam asti satyaṃ na tad yac chalam abhyupaiti
transliterated_devanagari: न सा सभा यत्र न सन्ति वृद्धा वृद्धा न ते ये न वदन्ति धर्मम् | धर्मः स नो यत्र न सत्यम् अस्ति सत्यं न तद् यच् छलम् अभ्युपइति
full_translation: That is not an assembly where there are no elders; they who do not speak the truth are not truthful. Where there is no truth, that is not accepted as deceit.

original_iast: yato rājadharmaś caiṣaḥ- dūto mleccho 'py avadhyaḥ syād rājā dūta-mukho yataḥ | udyateṣv api śastreṣu dūto vadati nānyathā
transliterated_devanagari: यतो राजधर्मश् चइषः- दूतो म्लेच्छो ऽप्य् अवध्यः स्याद् राजा दूत-मुखो यतः | उद्यतेष्व् अपि शस्त्रेषु दूतो वदति नान्यथा
full_translation: Wherever the kingly duty is, this messenger, even if he is a barbarian, should not be killed. The king's messenger, from whom weapons also rise, speaks as a messenger and not otherwise.

original_iast: anyac ca- svāpakarṣaṃ parotkarṣaṃ dūtoktair manyate tu kaḥ | sadaivāvadhya-bhāvena dūtaḥ sarvaṃ hi jalpati
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- स्वापकर्षं परोत्कर्षं दूतोक्तइर् मन्यते तु कः | सदइवावध्य-भावेन दूतः सर्वं हि जल्पति

word_by_word_translation.translation: always in a state of awareness

full_translation: And also, the attraction of sleep and the exaltation of others, as stated by the messenger, is considered; but who, indeed, speaks everything in a state of awareness, the messenger?

original_iast: asantuṣṭā dvijā naṣṭāḥ santuṣṭāś ca mahībhṛtaḥ | salajjā gaṇikā naṣṭā nirlajjāś ca kulāṅganā
transliterated_devanagari: असन्तुष्टा द्विजा नष्टाः सन्तुष्टाश् च महीभृतः | सलज्जा गणिका नष्टा निर्लज्जाश् च कुलाङ्गना

word_by_word_translation.translation: earth-holders, referring to kings or rulers
of noble lineage, referring to women of good family

full_translation: The unsatisfied twice-born have been destroyed, while the satisfied earth-holders are shy; the courtesans have been destroyed, and the shameless women of noble lineage.

original_iast: mitrāmātya-suhṛd-vargā yadā syur dṛḍha-bhaktayaḥ | śatrūṇāṃ viparītāś ca kartavyo vigrahas tadā
transliterated_devanagari: मित्रामात्य-सुहृद-वर्गा यदा स्युर् दृढ-भक्तयः | शत्रूणां विपरीताश् च कर्तव्यो विग्रहस् तदा
full_translation: When the friends and ministers, well-wishers, and groups are firmly devoted, and the enemies are in opposition, then conflict must be undertaken.

original_iast: anyac ca- bhūmir mitraṃ hiraṇyaṃ ca vigrahasya phalaṃ trayam | yadaitan niścitaṃ bhāvi kartavyo vigrahas tadā
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- भूमिर् मित्रं हिरण्यं च विग्रहस्य फलं त्रयम् | यदइतन् निश्चितं भावि कर्तव्यो विग्रहस् तदा
full_translation: And also, the earth, friend, and gold are the three fruits of the form, which is certain to be done in the future.

original_iast: viśanti sahasā mūḍhā ye'vicārya dviṣad-balam | khaḍga-dhārā-pariṣvaṅgaṃ labhante te suniścitam
transliterated_devanagari: विशन्ति सहसा मूढा येऽविचार्य द्विषद-बलम् | खड्ग-धारा-परिष्वङ्गं लभन्ते ते सुनिश्चितम्
full_translation: Those fools who suddenly enter without consideration, holding the twofold strength of the sword, certainly obtain an embrace.

original_iast: kiṃ mantreṇānanuṣṭhāne śāstravit pṛthivī-pateḥ | na hy auṣadha-parijñānād vyādheḥ śāntiḥ kvacid bhavet
transliterated_devanagari: किं मन्त्रेणाननुष्ठाने शास्त्रवित् पृथिवी-पतेः | न ह्य् औषध-परिज्ञानाद् व्याधेः शान्तिः क्वचिद् भवेत्
full_translation: What peace from disease can be found anywhere, indeed, without the performance of a mantra by one knowledgeable in scriptures, O lord of the earth?

original_iast: nady-adri-vana-durgeṣu yatra yatra bhayaṃ nṛpa | tatra tatra ca senānīr yāyād vyūhīkṛtair balaiḥ
transliterated_devanagari: नद्य-अद्रि-वन-दुर्गेषु यत्र यत्र भयं नृप | तत्र तत्र च सेनानीर् यायाद् व्यूहीकृतइर् बलइः
full_translation: Wherever there are rivers, mountains, forests, and fortresses, and wherever fear exists for the king, there the commander should go, having arranged the forces.

original_iast: balādhyakṣaḥ puro yāyāt pravīra-puruṣānvitaḥ | madhye kalatraṃ svāmī ca kośaḥ phalgu ca yad balam
transliterated_devanagari: बलाध्यक्षः पुरो यायात् प्रवीर-पुरुषान्वितः | मध्ये कलत्रं स्वामी च कोशः फल्गु च यद् बलम्
full_translation: The chief of strength may go forward, accompanied by valiant men, in the midst of his wife, the lord, and the treasure, which is fruitful in strength.

original_iast: pārśvayor ubhayor aśvā aśvānāṃ pārśvato rathāḥ | rathānāṃ pārśvato nāgā nāgānāṃ ca padātayaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: पार्श्वयोर् उभयोर् अश्वा अश्वानां पार्श्वतो रथाः | रथानां पार्श्वतो नागा नागानां च पदातयः
full_translation: On both sides, there are horses beside the horses, chariots beside the chariots, elephants beside the elephants, and infantry.

original_iast: paścāt senāpatir yāyāt khinnānāśvāsayan chanaiḥ | mantribhiḥ subhaṭair yuktaḥ pratigṛhya balaṃ nṛpaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: पश्चात् सेनापतिर् यायात् खिन्नानाश्वासयन् छनइः | मन्त्रिभिः सुभटइर् युक्तः प्रतिगृह्य बलं नृपः
full_translation: Afterwards, the commander should go, comforting the sorrowful, accompanied by the ministers, equipped with good warriors, having received the army, the king.

original_iast: sameyād viṣamaṃ nāgair jalāḍhyaṃ samahīdharam | samam aśvair jalaṃ nīmiḥ sarvatraiva padātibhiḥ
transliterated_devanagari: समेयाद् विषमं नागइर् जलाढ्यं समहीधरम् | समम् अश्वइर् जलं नीमिः सर्वत्रइव पदातिभिः
full_translation: From the same source, the uneven water-rich serpent equally holds the water of the horse, and the neem tree is everywhere by the foot soldiers.

original_iast: hastināṃ gamanaṃ proktaṃ praśastaṃ jaladāgame | tad anyatra turaṅgāṇāṃ pattīnāṃ sarvadaiva hi
transliterated_devanagari: हस्तिनां गमनं प्रोक्तं प्रशस्तं जलदागमे | तद् अन्यत्र तुरङ्गाणां पत्तीनां सर्वदइव हि
full_translation: The movement of elephants is declared praiseworthy in the arrival of clouds; that is, elsewhere, the wings of horses are certainly always so.

original_iast: śaileṣu durga-mārgeṣu vidheyaṃ nṛpa-rakṣaṇam | sva-yodhai rakṣitasyāpi śayanaṃ yoga-nidrayā
transliterated_devanagari: शइलेषु दुर्ग-मार्गेषु विधेयं नृप-रक्षणम् | स्व-योधइ रक्षितस्यापि शयनं योग-निद्रया
full_translation: In the mountains, on the paths of fortresses, the protection of the king should be established, even the rest of the protected by his own warriors through the practice of yoga and sleep.

original_iast: nāśayet karṣayec chatrūn durga-kaṇṭaka-mardanaiḥ | para-deśa-praveśe ca kuryād āṭavikān puraḥ
transliterated_devanagari: नाशयेत् कर्षयेच् छत्रून् दुर्ग-कण्टक-मर्दनइः | पर-देश-प्रवेशे च कुर्याद् आटविकान् पुरः
full_translation: One should destroy the enemies by cultivating the fortress, crushing the thorns, and upon entering a foreign country, should deal with the forest dwellers beforehand.

original_iast: yatra rājā tatra kośo vinā kośaṃ na rājatā | subhaṭebhyas tato dadyāt ko hi dātur na yudhyate
transliterated_devanagari: यत्र राजा तत्र कोशो विना कोशं न राजता | सुभटेभ्यस् ततो दद्यात् को हि दातुर् न युध्यते
full_translation: Where there is a king, there is a treasury; without a treasury, there is no royalty. Therefore, who indeed is a giver that does not fight?

original_iast: yataḥ- na narasya naro dāso dāsas tv arthasya bhūpate | gauravaṃ lāghavaṃ vāpi dhanādhana-nibandhanam
transliterated_devanagari: यतः- न नरस्य नरो दासो दासस् त्व् अर्थस्य भूपते | गउरवं लाघवं वापि धनाधन-निबन्धनम्
full_translation: From which, neither a man nor a servant, O lord of the earth, is bound by the heaviness or lightness of wealth and poverty.

original_iast: abhedena ca yudhyeta rakṣec caiva parasparam | phalgu sainyaṃ ca yat kiṃcin madhye vyūhasya kārayet
transliterated_devanagari: अभेदेन च युध्येत रक्षेच् चइव परस्परम् | फल्गु सइन्यं च यत् किंचिन् मध्ये व्यूहस्य कारयेत्
full_translation: One should fight without division, and also protect mutually; an army that is fruitful should create anything in the midst of the formation.

original_iast: padātīṃś ca mahīpālaḥ puro 'nīkasya yojayet | uparudhyārim āsīta rāṣṭraṃ cāsyopapīḍayet
transliterated_devanagari: पदातींश् च महीपालः पुरो ऽनीकस्य योजयेत् | उपरुध्यारिम् आसीत राष्ट्रं चास्योपपीडयेत्
full_translation: The king of the earth should arrange the foot soldiers in front of the army and was to oppress the enemy who is obstructing the nation.

original_iast: syandanāśvaiḥ same yudhyed anūpe nau-dvipais tathā | vṛkṣa-gulmāvṛte cāpair asi-carmāyudhaiḥ sthale
transliterated_devanagari: स्यन्दनाश्वइः समे युध्येद् अनूपे नउ-द्विपइस् तथा | वृक्ष-गुल्मावृते चापइर् असि-चर्मायुधइः स्थले
full_translation: You should fight equally on the battlefield with chariots and horses, nine elephants, and surrounded by trees and shrubs, with bows and leather weapons on the ground.

original_iast: dūṣayec cāsya satataṃ yavasān nodakendhanam | bhindyāc caiva taḍāgāni prakārārān parikhās tathā
transliterated_devanagari: दूषयेच् चास्य सततं यवसान् नोदकेन्धनम् | भिन्द्याच् चइव तडागानि प्रकारारान् परिखास् तथा
full_translation: "May it constantly corrupt the harvest of this water fuel, may it also break the ponds of various types and their boundaries."

original_iast: baleṣu pramukho hastī na tathānyo mahīpateḥ | nijair avayavair eva mātaṅgo 'ṣṭāyudhaḥ smṛtaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: बलेषु प्रमुखो हस्ती न तथान्यो महीपतेः | निजइर् अवयवइर् एव मातङ्गो ऽष्टायुधः स्मृतः

word_by_word_translation.translation: of the king of the earth

full_translation: In terms of strength, the elephant is foremost; it is not so for others. Indeed, the elephant, with its own limbs, is remembered as the eight-armed one of the king of the earth.

original_iast: balam aśvaś ca sainyānāṃ prākāro jaṅgamo yataḥ | tasmād aśvādhiko rājā vijayī sthala-vigrahe
transliterated_devanagari: बलम् अश्वश् च सइन्यानां प्राकारो जङ्गमो यतः | तस्माद् अश्वाधिको राजा विजयी स्थल-विग्रहे
full_translation: The strength of the armies, which is mobile and fortified, is greater than that of horses; therefore, the king is victorious in battle.

original_iast: tathā coktam- yudhyamānā hayārūḍhā devānām api durjayāḥ | api dūrasthitās teṣāṃ vairiṇo hastavattinaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: तथा चोक्तम- युध्यमाना हयारूढा देवानाम् अपि दुर्जयाः | अपि दूरस्थितास् तेषां वइरिणो हस्तवत्तिनः
full_translation: Thus it is said that those who are fighting, mounted on horses, are also difficult to conquer, even those who are far away, with powerful hands of the enemies.

original_iast: prathamaṃ yuddha-kāritvaṃ samasta-bala-pālanam | diṅ-mārgāṇāṃ viśodhitvaṃ patti-karma pracakṣate
transliterated_devanagari: प्रथमं युद्ध-कारित्वं समस्त-बल-पालनम् | दिङ-मार्गाणां विशोधित्वं पत्ति-कर्म प्रचक्षते
full_translation: The first action of war is the protection of all forces, the purification of the directions, and the declaration of the action of the fall.

original_iast: svabhāva-śūram astrajñam aviraktaṃ jita-śramam | prasiddha-kṣatriya-prāyaṃ balaṃ śreṣṭhatamaṃ viduḥ
transliterated_devanagari: स्वभाव-शूरम् अस्त्रज्ञम् अविरक्तं जित-श्रमम् | प्रसिद्ध-क्षत्रिय-प्रायं बलं श्रेष्ठतमं विदुः
full_translation: They know that a Kshatriya is generally the best in nature, brave, knowledgeable in weapons, unattached, having conquered effort, and renowned for his strength.

original_iast: yathā prabhu-kṛtān mānād yudhyante bhuvi mānavāḥ | na tathā bahubhir dattair draviṇair api bhūpate
transliterated_devanagari: यथा प्रभु-कृतान् मानाद् युध्यन्ते भुवि मानवाः | न तथा बहुभिर् दत्तइर् द्रविणइर् अपि भूपते
full_translation: Just as humans fight on earth out of respect for the lord, they do not do so merely for the wealth given by many to the king.

original_iast: varam alpa-balaṃ sāraṃ na kuryān muṇḍa-maṇḍalīm | kuryād asāra-bhaṅgo hi sāra-bhaṅgam api sphuṭam
transliterated_devanagari: वरम् अल्प-बलं सारं न कुर्यान् मुण्ड-मण्डलीम् | कुर्याद् असार-भङ्गो हि सार-भङ्गम् अपि स्फुटम्
full_translation: One should not create a circle of little strength; indeed, a break of the worthless is also a clear break of the essence.

original_iast: aprasādo 'nadhiṣṭhānaṃ deyāṃśa-haraṇaṃ ca yat | kāla-yāpo 'pratīkāras tad vairāgyasya kāraṇam
transliterated_devanagari: अप्रसादो ऽनधिष्ठानं देयांश-हरणं च यत् | काल-यापो ऽप्रतीकारस् तद् वइराग्यस्य कारणम्
full_translation: The lack of grace and foundation, the taking away of offerings, and that which is the duration of time without counteraction—these are the causes of renunciation.

original_iast: apīḍayan balaṃ śatrūñ jigīṣur abhiṣeṇayet | sukha-sādhyaṃ dviṣāṃ sainyaṃ dīrgha-prayāṇa-pīḍitam
transliterated_devanagari: अपीडयन् बलं शत्रूञ् जिगीषुर् अभिषेणयेत् | सुख-साध्यं द्विषां सइन्यं दीर्घ-प्रयाण-पीडितम्

word_by_word_translation.translation: the one who desires to conquer

full_translation: The one who desires to conquer should crush the strength of the enemies, achieving happiness that is attainable for the army of foes, which is afflicted during a long journey.

original_iast: dāyādād aparo yasmān nāsti bheda-karo dviṣām | tasmād utthāpayed yatnād dāyādaṃ tasya vidviṣaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: दायादाद् अपरो यस्मान् नास्ति भेद-करो द्विषाम् | तस्माद् उत्थापयेद् यत्नाद् दायादं तस्य विद्विषः
full_translation: Therefore, one should elevate the heir with effort, as there is no difference among the enemies from whom another heir does not arise.

original_iast: sandhāya yuvarājena yadi vā mukhya-mantriṇā | antaḥ-prakopaṇaṃ kuryād abhiyoktā sthirātmanaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: सन्धाय युवराजेन यदि वा मुख्य-मन्त्रिणा | अन्तः-प्रकोपणं कुर्याद् अभियोक्ता स्थिरात्मनः
full_translation: If the young prince or the chief minister were to provoke from within, the accuser of the steadfast-minded would act.

original_iast: krūrāmitraṃ raṇe cāpi bhaṅgaṃ dattvā vighātayet | athavā go-grahākṛṣṭyā tan-mukhyāśrita-bandhanāt
transliterated_devanagari: क्रूरामित्रं रणे चापि भङ्गं दत्त्वा विघातयेत् | अथवा गो-ग्रहाकृष्ट्या तन-मुख्याश्रित-बन्धनात्

word_by_word_translation.translation: by being drawn by the planet

full_translation: One should defeat a cruel enemy in battle, or destroy that which is mainly dependent on bondage, drawn by the influence of the planet (as if by a cow).

original_iast: svarājyaṃ vāsayed rājā para-deśāpaharaṇāt | athavā dāna-mānābhyāṃ vāsitaṃ dhanadaṃ hi tat
transliterated_devanagari: स्वराज्यं वासयेद् राजा पर-देशापहरणात् | अथवा दान-मानाभ्यां वासितं धनदं हि तत्
full_translation: The king should establish self-rule, either from foreign invasion or by the means of gifts and honor, for that indeed is wealth-giving.

original_iast: athavā bahunoditena- ātmodayaḥ para-glānir dvayaṃ nītir itīyatī | tad ūrīkṛtya kṛtibhir vācaspatyaṃ pratīyate
transliterated_devanagari: अथवा बहुनोदितेन- आत्मोदयः पर-ग्लानिर् द्वयं नीतिर् इतीयती | तद् ऊरीकृत्य कृतिभिर् वाचस्पत्यं प्रतीयते
full_translation: Or, through extensive discussion, self-awakening is said to be the twofold policy of decline; having elaborated that, it is perceived by the creators of speech.

original_iast: anyad ucchṛṅkhalaṃ sattvam anyac chāstra-niyantritam | sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ hi tejas-timirayoḥ kutaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यद् उच्छृङ्खलं सत्त्वम् अन्यच् छास्त्र-नियन्त्रितम् | सामानाधिकरण्यं हि तेजस-तिमिरयोः कुतः
full_translation: Another entity is uncontrolled, while another is controlled by scripture; indeed, whence is the commonality of light and darkness?

original_iast: paro 'pi hitavān bandhur bandhur apy ahitaḥ paraḥ | ahito dehajo vyādhir hitam āraṇyam auṣadham
transliterated_devanagari: परो ऽपि हितवान् बन्धुर् बन्धुर् अप्य् अहितः परः | अहितो देहजो व्याधिर् हितम् आरण्यम् औषधम्
full_translation: Even another friend can be beneficial, while another may be harmful; a disease that arises from the body can be harmful, but the forest is a source of beneficial herbs.

original_iast: aparaṃ ca- āsīd vīra-varo nāma śūdrakasya mahībhṛtaḥ | sevakaḥ svalpa-kālena sa dadau sutam ātmanaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अपरं च- आसीद् वीर-वरो नाम शूद्रकस्य महीभृतः | सेवकः स्वल्प-कालेन स ददउ सुतम् आत्मनः
full_translation: There was another brave best named Shudraka, a servant of the earth-holder, who, in a short time, gave a son of himself.

original_iast: dhanāni jīvitaṃ caiva parārthe prājña utsṛjet | tan-nimitto varaṃ tyāgo vināśe niyate sati
transliterated_devanagari: धनानि जीवितं चइव परार्थे प्राज्ञ उत्सृजेत् | तन-निमित्तो वरं त्यागो विनाशे नियते सति
full_translation: A wise person should indeed give up wealth and life for the sake of others; it is better to renounce that which is a cause of destruction when one is determined.

original_iast: jāyante ca mriyante ca mad-vidhāḥ kṣudra-jantavaḥ | anena sadṛśo loke na bhūto na bhaviṣyati
transliterated_devanagari: जायन्ते च म्रियन्ते च मद-विधाः क्षुद्र-जन्तवः | अनेन सदृशो लोके न भूतो न भविष्यति
full_translation: Small beings, similar to this, are born and die; such creatures have neither existed in the past nor will they exist in the future.

original_iast: priyaṃ brūyād akṛpaṇaḥ śūraḥ syād avikatthanaḥ | dātā nāpātra-varṣī ca pragalbhaḥ syād aniṣṭhuraḥ
transliterated_devanagari: प्रियं ब्रूयाद् अकृपणः शूरः स्याद् अविकत्थनः | दाता नापात्र-वर्षी च प्रगल्भः स्याद् अनिष्ठुरः
full_translation: One should speak kindly; a brave person should not be miserly, should not be talkative, should be a generous giver, should not be unworthy, should give abundantly, should be mature, and should not be harsh.

original_iast: cakravāko brūte- yo 'kāryaṃ kāryavac chāsti sa kiṃ mantrī nṛpecchayā | varaṃ svāmi-mano-duḥkhaṃ tan-nāśo na tv akāryataḥ
transliterated_devanagari: चक्रवाको ब्रूते- यो ऽकार्यं कार्यवच् छास्ति स किं मन्त्री नृपेच्छया | वरं स्वामि-मनो-दुःखं तन-नाशो न त्व् अकार्यतः
full_translation: The Chakravāka says: "Who, being unaccomplished, exists as the word of action? What minister, by the desire of the king, is the best? O lord, the mind suffers; the body does not perish due to inaction."

original_iast: vaidyo guruś ca mantrī ca yasya rājñaḥ priyaṃvadāḥ | śarīra-dharma-kośebhyaḥ kṣipraṃ sa parihīyate
transliterated_devanagari: वइद्यो गुरुश् च मन्त्री च यस्य राज्ञः प्रियंवदाः | शरीर-धर्म-कोशेभ्यः क्षिप्रं स परिहीयते
full_translation: The knowledgeable teacher and the minister, whose beloved words are the body of dharma, are quickly removed from the treasury of the king.

original_iast: śṛṇu deva ! puṇyāl labdhaṃ yad ekena tan mamāpi bhaviṣyati | hatvā bhikṣuṃ yato mohān nidhy-arthī nāpito hataḥ
transliterated_devanagari: शृणु देव ! पुण्याल् लब्धं यद् एकेन तन् ममापि भविष्यति | हत्वा भिक्षुं यतो मोहान् निध्य-अर्थी नापितो हतः
full_translation: Listen, O God, that which is obtained by the virtuous, will also happen to me if, having killed the beggar, the seeker of wealth is not killed from the delusions.

original_iast: rājāha- purāvṛtta-kathodgāraiḥ kathaṃ nirṇīyate paraḥ | syān niṣkāraṇa-bandhur vā kiṃ vā viśvāsa-ghātakaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: राजाह- पुरावृत्त-कथोद्गारइः कथं निर्णीयते परः | स्यान् निष्कारण-बन्धुर् वा किं वा विश्वास-घातकः
full_translation: How is it decided by the ancient stories narrated by the king, whether the other may be a friend without cause, or what, or a betrayer of trust?

original_iast: lubdhaḥ krūro 'laso 'satyaḥ pramādī bhīrur asthiraḥ | mūḍho yodhāvamantā ca sukha-cchedyo ripuḥ smṛtaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: लुब्धः क्रूरो ऽलसो ऽसत्यः प्रमादी भीरुर् अस्थिरः | मूढो योधावमन्ता च सुख-च्छेद्यो रिपुः स्मृतः
full_translation: The greedy, cruel, lazy, untruthful, careless, timid, unstable, foolish warrior who does not speak is remembered as an enemy to be cut off from happiness.

original_iast: dīrgha-vartma-pariśrāntaṃ nady-adri-vana-saṅkulam | ghorāgni-bhaya-santrastaṃ kṣut-pipāsārditaṃ tathā
transliterated_devanagari: दीर्घ-वर्त्म-परिश्रान्तं नद्य-अद्रि-वन-सङ्कुलम् | घोराग्नि-भय-सन्त्रस्तं क्षुत-पिपासार्दितं तथा
full_translation: A long path, weary from the rivers, filled with mountains and forests, is terrified by a terrible fire, frightened by fear, tormented by hunger and thirst.

original_iast: pramattaṃ bhojana-vyagraṃ vyādhi-durbhikṣa-pīḍitam | asaṃsthitam abhūyiṣṭhaṃ vṛṣṭi-vāta-samākulam
transliterated_devanagari: प्रमत्तं भोजन-व्यग्रं व्याधि-दुर्भिक्ष-पीडितम् | असंस्थितम् अभूयिष्ठं वृष्टि-वात-समाकुलम्
full_translation: Distracted by food, busy with disease, afflicted by famine, unstable, most distressed by rain and disturbed by wind.

original_iast: paṅka-pāṃśu-jalācchannaṃ suvyastaṃ dasyu-vidrutam | evambhūtaṃ mahīpālaḥ para-sainyaṃ vighātayet
transliterated_devanagari: पङ्क-पांशु-जलाच्छन्नं सुव्यस्तं दस्यु-विद्रुतम् | एवम्भूतं महीपालः पर-सइन्यं विघातयेत्
full_translation: Thus, the king of the earth, being well-arranged and covered by water with mud and dust, should destroy the fleeing thief and the other army.

original_iast: anyac ca- avaskanda-bhayād rājā prajāgara-kṛta-śramam | divā-suptaṃ sadā hanyān nidrā-vyākula-sainikam
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- अवस्कन्द-भयाद् राजा प्रजागर-कृत-श्रमम् | दिवा-सुप्तं सदा हन्यान् निद्रा-व्याकुल-सइनिकम्
full_translation: And also, due to fear of falling, the king awoke from his labor during the day, always ready to kill the disturbed sleep of the army.

original_iast: na rājyaṃ prāptam ity eva vartitavyam asāmpratam | śriyaṃ hy avinayo hanti jarā rūpam ivottamam
transliterated_devanagari: न राज्यं प्राप्तम् इत्य् एव वर्तितव्यम् असाम्प्रतम् | श्रियं ह्य् अविनयो हन्ति जरा रूपम् इवोत्तमम्
full_translation: One should only live as if one has not obtained a kingdom; indeed, a lack of humility destroys prosperity, just like old age destroys an excellent form.

original_iast: api ca- dakṣaḥ śriyam adhigacchati pathy āśī kalyatāṃ sukham arogī | udyukto viyāntaṃ dharmārtha-yaśāṃsi ca vinītaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अपि च- दक्षः श्रियम् अधिगच्छति पथ्य् आशी कल्यतां सुखम् अरोगी | उद्युक्तो वियान्तं धर्मार्थ-यशांसि च विनीतः
full_translation: Moreover, a skilled person attains prosperity through the right blessings, experiences happiness and well-being, remains healthy, is prepared for departure, and humbly acquires righteousness, wealth, and fame.

original_iast: gṛdhro 'vadat-deva ! śṛṇu- avidvān api bhū-pālo vidyā-vṛddhopasevayā | parāṃ śriyam avāpnoti jalāsanna-tarur yathā
transliterated_devanagari: गृध्रो ऽवदत-देव ! शृणु- अविद्वान् अपि भू-पालो विद्या-वृद्धोपसेवया | परां श्रियम् अवाप्नोति जलासन्न-तरुर् यथा
full_translation: The vulture said, "O deity, listen! Even the ignorant protector of the earth attains supreme wealth by serving the elderly, just as a tree near water does."

original_iast: anyac ca- pāpaṃ strī mṛgayā dyūtam artha-dūṣaṇam eva ca | vāg-daṇḍayoś ca pāruṣyaṃ vyasanāni mahībhujām
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- पापं स्त्री मृगया द्यूतम् अर्थ-दूषणम् एव च | वाग-दण्डयोश् च पारुष्यं व्यसनानि महीभुजाम्
full_translation: And also, the sins of women include hunting, gambling, the corruption of wealth, indeed, harshness of speech, punishments, and addictions of the powerful.

original_iast: na sāhasaikānta-rasānuvartinā na cāpy upāyopahatāntarātmanā | vibhūtayaḥ śakyam avāptum ūrjitā naye ca śaurye ca vasanti sampadaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: न साहसइकान्त-रसानुवर्तिना न चाप्य् उपायोपहतान्तरात्मना | विभूतयः शक्यम् अवाप्तुम् ऊर्जिता नये च शउर्ये च वसन्ति सम्पदः
full_translation: In solitude, not even the essence of courage can be attained by those afflicted by the inner self; glories cannot be achieved. Energized in the path of bravery, prosperities dwell.

original_iast: santāpayanti kam apathya-bhujaṃ na rogāḥ ? kaṃ śrīr na darpayati kaṃ na nihanti mṛtyuḥ kaṃ strī-kṛtā na viṣayāḥ paritāpayanti
transliterated_devanagari: सन्तापयन्ति कम् अपथ्य-भुजं न रोगाः ? कं श्रीर् न दर्पयति कं न निहन्ति मृत्युः कं स्त्री-कृता न विषयाः परितापयन्ति
full_translation: Who does not torment with unwholesome food? Who do diseases not affect? Whom does prosperity not arrogate? Whom does death not kill? Whom does a woman not torment with her desires?

original_iast: mudaṃ viṣādaḥ śaradaṃ himāgamas tamo vivasvān sukṛtaṃ kṛtaghnatā | priyopapattiḥ śucam āpadaṃ nayaḥ śriyaḥ samṛddhā api hanti durnayaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: मुदं विषादः शरदं हिमागमस् तमो विवस्वान् सुकृतं कृतघ्नता | प्रियोपपत्तिः शुचम् आपदं नयः श्रियः समृद्धा अपि हन्ति दुर्नयः
full_translation: Joy and sorrow, the arrival of winter in autumn, darkness, the sun, good deeds, ingratitude, beloved outcomes, purity, calamity, guidance, prosperity, even the prosperous can be destroyed by bad conduct.

original_iast: devatāsu gurau goṣu rājasu brāhmaṇeṣu ca | niyantavyaḥ sadā kopo bāla-vṛddhātureṣu ca
transliterated_devanagari: देवतासु गुरउ गोषु राजसु ब्राह्मणेषु च | नियन्तव्यः सदा कोपो बाल-वृद्धातुरेषु च
full_translation: One should always control anger towards the deities, teachers, cows, kings, and Brahmins, as well as towards children, the elderly, and the sick.

original_iast: mantriṇāṃ bhinna-sandhāne bhiṣajāṃ sāṃnipātike | karmaṇi vyajyate prajñā susthe ko vā na paṇḍitaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: मन्त्रिणां भिन्न-सन्धाने भिषजां सांनिपातिके | कर्मणि व्यज्यते प्रज्ञा सुस्थे को वा न पण्डितः
full_translation: In the agreements of different ministers, the wisdom of physicians is revealed in the treatment; who among the healthy is not learned?

original_iast: aparaṃ ca- ārambhante'lpam evājñāḥ kāmaṃ vyagrā bhavanti ca | mahārambhāḥ kṛta-dhiyas tiṣṭhanti ca nirākulāḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अपरं च- आरम्भन्तेऽल्पम् एवाज्ञाः कामं व्यग्रा भवन्ति च | महारम्भाः कृत-धियस् तिष्ठन्ति च निराकुलाः
full_translation: Another begins indeed with a little command; desires become distracted, and great undertakings are accomplished by intellects that stand unperturbed.

original_iast: yaḥ kākiṇīm apy apatha-prapannāṃ samuddharen niṣka-sahasra-tulyām | kāleṣu koṭiṣv api mukta-hastas taṃ rāja-siṃhaṃ na jahāti lakṣmīḥ
transliterated_devanagari: यः काकिणीम् अप्य् अपथ-प्रपन्नां समुद्धरेन् निष्क-सहस्र-तुल्याम् | कालेषु कोटिष्व् अपि मुक्त-हस्तस् तं राज-सिंहं न जहाति लक्ष्मीः
full_translation: Whoever, even if a crow takes refuge on the wrong path, will uplift a thousand coins equal in value; in times of crores, even if free-handed, that lion-king is not forsaken by Lakshmi.

original_iast: kratau vivāhe vyasane ripu-kṣaye yaśaskare karmaṇi mitra-saṅgrahe | priyāsu nārīṣv adhaneṣu bāndhaveṣv ativyayo nāsti narādhipāṣṭasu
transliterated_devanagari: क्रतउ विवाहे व्यसने रिपु-क्षये यशस्करे कर्मणि मित्र-सङ्ग्रहे | प्रियासु नारीष्व् अधनेषु बान्धवेष्व् अतिव्ययो नास्ति नराधिपाष्टसु

word_by_word_translation.translation: in the act of gaining fame

full_translation: In the context of sacrifice, marriage, adversity, the destruction of enemies, the act of gaining fame through deeds, gathering friends, among beloved ones, among women, among the wealthy, among relatives, there is no excessive expenditure in the realm of the king.

original_iast: yataḥ- mūrkhaḥ svalpa-vyaya-trāsāt sarvanāśaṃ karoti hi | kaḥ sudhīḥ santyajed bhāṇḍaṃ śuklasyaivātisādhvasāt
transliterated_devanagari: यतः- मूर्खः स्वल्प-व्यय-त्रासात् सर्वनाशं करोति हि | कः सुधीः सन्त्यजेद् भाण्डं शुक्लस्यइवातिसाध्वसात्
full_translation: Indeed, who would abandon a vessel of the white, when a fool causes total destruction from a small expenditure due to fear?

original_iast: parasparajñāḥ saṃhṛṣṭās tyaktuṃ prāṇān suniścitāḥ | kulīnāḥ pūjitāḥ samyag vijayante dviṣad-balam
transliterated_devanagari: परस्परज्ञाः संहृष्टास् त्यक्तुं प्राणान् सुनिश्चिताः | कुलीनाः पूजिताः सम्यग् विजयन्ते द्विषद-बलम्
full_translation: Mutually knowledgeable and delighted, the noble ones, who are ensured to give up their lives, are rightly worshipped and conquer the strength of their enemies.

original_iast: aparaṃ ca- subhaṭāḥ śīla-sampannāḥ saṃhatāḥ kṛta-niścayāḥ | api pañca-śataṃ śūrā nighnanti ripu-vāhinīm
transliterated_devanagari: अपरं च- सुभटाः शील-सम्पन्नाः संहताः कृत-निश्चयाः | अपि पञ्च-शतं शूरा निघ्नन्ति रिपु-वाहिनीम्
full_translation: Moreover, even five hundred brave warriors, endowed with good character and united with determination, strike down the enemy army.

original_iast: kiṃ ca- śiṣṭair apy avaśeṣajña ugraś ca kṛta-nāśakaḥ | tyajyate kiṃ punar nānyair yaś cāpy ātmambharir naraḥ
transliterated_devanagari: किं च- शिष्टइर् अप्य् अवशेषज्ञ उग्रश् च कृत-नाशकः | त्यज्यते किं पुनर् नान्यइर् यश् चाप्य् आत्मम्भरिर् नरः
full_translation: What then, even by the learned, is the fierce destroyer that is abandoned? What again, is there that is not by others, even a self-reliant man?

original_iast: yataḥ- satyaṃ śauryaṃ dayā tyāgo nṛpasyaite mahā-guṇāḥ | etais tyakto mahīpālaḥ prāpnoti khalu vācyatām
transliterated_devanagari: यतः- सत्यं शउर्यं दया त्यागो नृपस्यइते महा-गुणाः | एतइस् त्यक्तो महीपालः प्राप्नोति खलु वाच्यताम्
full_translation: From which, truth, bravery, compassion, and sacrifice are the great qualities of the king; indeed, by abandoning these, the ruler of the earth attains [a state that can be said].

original_iast: yo yena pratibaddhaḥ syāt saha tenodayī vyayī | sa viśvasto niyoktavyaḥ prāṇeṣu ca dhaneṣu ca
transliterated_devanagari: यो येन प्रतिबद्धः स्यात् सह तेनोदयी व्ययी | स विश्वस्तो नियोक्तव्यः प्राणेषु च धनेषु च
full_translation: Whoever is bound by someone, he should be appointed as a trustworthy expenditure in both life and wealth.

original_iast: yataḥ- dhūrtaḥ strī vā śiśur yasya mantriṇaḥ syur mahīpateḥ | anīti-pavana-kṣipto 'kāryābdhau sa nimajjati
transliterated_devanagari: यतः- धूर्तः स्त्री वा शिशुर् यस्य मन्त्रिणः स्युर् महीपतेः | अनीति-पवन-क्षिप्तो ऽकार्याब्धउ स निमज्जति
full_translation: From which unrighteousness of the king, the cunning woman or child, whose ministers may be cast by the wind, he sinks in the ocean of inaction.

original_iast: śṛṇu deva! - harṣa-krodhau yatau yasya śāstrārthe pratyayas tathā | nityaṃ bhṛtyānupekṣā ca tasya syād dhanadā dharā
transliterated_devanagari: शृणु देव! - हर्ष-क्रोधउ यतउ यस्य शास्त्रार्थे प्रत्ययस् तथा | नित्यं भृत्यानुपेक्षा च तस्य स्याद् धनदा धरा
full_translation: O God, listen! Joy and anger are that which, in the purpose of scriptures, brings certainty. Always consider the servants, for of him may the earth be wealth-giving.

original_iast: yeṣāṃ rājñā saha syātām uccayāpacayau dhruvam | amātyā iti tān rājā nāvamanyet kadācana
transliterated_devanagari: येषां राज्ञा सह स्याताम् उच्चयापचयउ ध्रुवम् | अमात्या इति तान् राजा नावमन्येत् कदाचन
full_translation: The king should not disrespect those who are together with him, certainly by the ministers, whether they are high or low, at any time.

original_iast: mahībhujo madāndhasya saṅkīrṇasyeva dantinaḥ | skhalato hi karālambaḥ suśiṣṭair eva kīyate
transliterated_devanagari: महीभुजो मदान्धस्य सङ्कीर्णस्येव दन्तिनः | स्खलतो हि करालम्बः सुशिष्टइर् एव कीयते
full_translation: Indeed, the fearsome one, who is of the earth-possessor, the intoxicated, and the confused, is measured with well-ordered slips.

original_iast: viṣamo 'pi yathā nakraḥ salilān nisṛto vaśaḥ | vanād vinirgataḥ śūraḥ siṃho 'pi syāc chagālavat
transliterated_devanagari: विषमो ऽपि यथा नक्रः सलिलान् निसृतो वशः | वनाद् विनिर्गतः शूरः सिंहो ऽपि स्याच् छगालवत्
full_translation: Even though it is uneven, just as a crocodile emerges from the waters under control, a brave lion may also exit from the forest like a goat.

original_iast: puraskṛtya balaṃ rājā yodhayed avalokayan | svāminādhiṣṭhitaḥ śvāpi kiṃ na siṃhāyate dhruvam
transliterated_devanagari: पुरस्कृत्य बलं राजा योधयेद् अवलोकयन् | स्वामिनाधिष्ठितः श्वापि किं न सिंहायते ध्रुवम्
full_translation: Having prepared strength, the king should engage in battle, observing the lord established; even a dog certainly does not refrain from roaring.

original_iast: akāla-sahamaty-alpaṃ mūrkha-vyasani-nāyakam | aguptaṃ bhīru-yodhaṃ ca durga-vyasanam ucyate
transliterated_devanagari: अकाल-सहमत्य-अल्पं मूर्ख-व्यसनि-नायकम् | अगुप्तं भीरु-योधं च दुर्ग-व्यसनम् उच्यते
full_translation: An untimely agreement with a little foolish leader, an unprotected cowardly warrior, is said to be a difficult calamity.

original_iast: upajāpaś cirārodho 'vaskandas tīvra-pauruṣam | durgasya laṅghanopāyāś catvāraḥ kathitā ime
transliterated_devanagari: उपजापश् चिरारोधो ऽवस्कन्दस् तीव्र-पउरुषम् | दुर्गस्य लङ्घनोपायाश् चत्वारः कथिता इमे
full_translation: These four methods of overcoming the long-lasting obstruction of the fortress with intense strength have been described.

original_iast: sumantritaṃ suvikrāntaṃ suyuddhaṃ supalāyitam | kārya-kāle yathā-śakti kuryān na tu vicārayet
transliterated_devanagari: सुमन्त्रितं सुविक्रान्तं सुयुद्धं सुपलायितम् | कार्य-काले यथा-शक्ति कुर्यान् न तु विचारयेत्
full_translation: One should act in accordance with their ability, as advised, well-advanced, well-fought, and well-supplied, at the right time, but should not deliberate.

original_iast: yadi samaram apāsya nāsti mṛtyor bhayam iti yuktam ito 'nyataḥ prayātum | atha maraṇam avaśyam eva jantoḥ kim iti mudhā malinaṃ yaśaḥ kriyate ?
transliterated_devanagari: यदि समरम् अपास्य नास्ति मृत्योर् भयम् इति युक्तम् इतो ऽन्यतः प्रयातुम् | अथ मरणम् अवश्यम् एव जन्तोः किम् इति मुधा मलिनं यशः क्रियते ?
full_translation: If one has abandoned battle, there is no fear of death; thus it is reasonable to go elsewhere. Then, what is certain is death for beings. Foolishly, impure fame is created.

original_iast: anyac ca- bhave'smin pavanodbhrānta-vīci-vibhrama-bhaṅgure | jāyate puṇay-yogena parārthe jīvita-vyayaḥ
transliterated_devanagari: अन्यच् च- भवेऽस्मिन् पवनोद्भ्रान्त-वीचि-विभ्रम-भङ्गुरे | जायते पुणय-योगेन परार्थे जीवित-व्ययः
full_translation: Also, in this existence, the disturbed waves of the wind arise, fragile, and the expenditure of life is for the sake of others through the means of merit and yoga.

original_iast: svāmy-amātyaś ca rāṣṭraṃ ca durgaṃ kośo balaṃ suhṛt | rājyāṅgāni prakṛtayaḥ paurāṇāṃ śreṇayo 'pi ca
transliterated_devanagari: स्वाम्य-अमात्यश् च राष्ट्रं च दुर्गं कोशो बलं सुहृत् | राज्याङ्गानि प्रकृतयः पउराणां श्रेणयो ऽपि च
